He made clear that He alone is the Helper, and not any other, and said: ﴿And upon God let the believers put their trust.﴾ Thus He forbade trusting in anyone other than Him and commanded trusting in Him, so that the one who trusts in Him may obtain the help that no one other than Him can give. Otherwise, the one who trusts in someone other than God seeks help from that one. If what is sought from that one does not come about, there is no meaning in mentioning that He alone gives help. For according to this view, His helping the one who trusts in Him is like His helping the one who does not trust in Him, and this contradicts the purpose of the verse. Rather, according to these people, He may help one who trusts in someone else and not help one who trusts in Him. So how could He command trusting in Him alone, to the exclusion of others, coupled with His saying: ﴿If God helps you, none can overcome you; but if He forsakes you, who is there that can help you after Him? And upon God let the believers put their trust.﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 160]

Similarly His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Is God not sufficient for His servant? Yet they frighten you with those other than Him. And whomever God leaves astray, there is no guide for him.﴾ [al-Zumar: 36] – up to His saying – ﴿Say: God is sufficient for me; upon Him let those who trust rely.﴾ [al-Zumar: 38] Thus He made clear that God suffices His servant who worships Him, who is one of His servants over whom Satan has no authority, who is one of His sincere servants, of the servants of the Most Merciful who walk upon the earth in humility. Similar to this is His saying: ﴿Glory be to Him who took His servant by night﴾ [al-Isra': 1], and His saying: ﴿And when the servant of God stood calling upon Him﴾ [al-Jinn: 19], [p-1913] and His saying: ﴿And if you are in doubt about what We have sent down upon Our servant﴾ [al-Baqarah: 23]. Similar examples are many. Then He commanded him with His saying: ﴿Say: God is sufficient for me; upon Him let those who trust rely.﴾ [al-Zumar: 38]

And God, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Recite to them the news of Noah, when he said to his people: "O my people, if my standing [among you] and my reminding you of God's signs is burdensome to you, then upon God I have relied. So resolve upon your affair with your associates, then let not your affair be obscure to you; then carry it out upon me and give me no respite."﴾ [Yunus: 71]

Likewise He related of Hud when his people said: ﴿We only say that some of our gods have struck you with evil.﴾ He said: ﴿I call God to witness, and bear witness yourselves, that I am free of what you associate﴾ [Hud: 54] ﴿with other than Him. So scheme against me all together, then give me no respite.﴾ [Hud: 55] ﴿Indeed, I have relied upon God, my Lord and your Lord. There is no creature but that He holds its forelock. Indeed, my Lord is on a straight path.﴾ [Hud: 56]

This is from the speech of the messengers, which shows that by his trust in God he repelled their evil from himself. Noah says: ﴿If my standing [among you] and my reminding you of God's signs is burdensome to you, then upon God I have relied﴾ [Yunus: 71], and so on. He summoned them, when they magnified what he was doing and were averse to it, to gather together and then do what they wished of destruction. He said: "Upon God I have relied." Had it not been that, by the reality of this word – namely his trust in God – He would overcome them in what he challenged them to, when he challenged them to a contest, he would have asked them to destroy him. This is not permissible, and it would be a request that they fail. So this indicates that, by his trust in God, He overcame them in what he challenged them to. Likewise Hud calls God, the Exalted, and them to witness that he is free of what they associate with God. Then he challenges them and overcomes them by his saying: ﴿So scheme against me all together﴾ [Hud: 55] ﴿then give me no respite﴾ [Hud: 55] ﴿Indeed, I have relied upon God, my Lord and your Lord. There is no creature but that He holds its forelock﴾ [Hud: 56]. This shows that he relied upon the One who holds the forelocks of humans and all beasts. So He will repel you from me because I am one who relies [p-1914] upon Him. Had the existence of trust been the same as its absence in this matter, he would have incited them to attack him, and mentioning his trust would have had no benefit. For the reality of the matter, according to these people, is that there is no difference between one who trusts and one who does not trust in the arrival of punishment to him, and they were more numerous and stronger than him, so they would have destroyed him.

And if he had said, "Indeed God is my protector and my helper," and similar words, it would have been known that he was reporting that God, may He be exalted, repels them, and He repels them because of his faith and piety, and because he is His servant and messenger. God is with His messenger and his allies. So when, because of faith and piety, God repels harm from the believing and God-fearing, it is known that the servant has inner and outer deeds by which benefit is brought and harm is averted, and trust in God is among the greatest of these. And it is known that whoever thinks that what is decreed of benefits and harms is not dependent upon causes, but occurs without them, is mistaken. Likewise, whoever makes these things mere signs and indicators, because one accompanies the other, has erred, for God has informed us that He does this with that in more than one place in the Qur'an, in creation and command. Such as His saying: ﴿Then We sent down water from it and brought forth thereby fruits of every kind﴾ [al-A'raf: 57], and His saying: ﴿Eat and drink with satisfaction for what you advanced in the days past﴾ [al-Haqqah: 24], and His saying: ﴿for what you used to do﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 105]. And He denounced those who think that the existence of causes is the same as their absence, in such sayings as: ﴿Shall We treat the Muslims like the criminals?﴾ [al-Qalam: 35], and His saying: ﴿Or shall We treat those who believe and do righteous deeds like corrupters upon the earth? Or shall We treat the righteous like the wicked?﴾ [Sad: 28], and similar verses.

These people (the Jabriyya, the determinists) say: "Command and prohibition, in reality, are merely an announcement that punishment will befall the disobedient purely by an act of will, not because of a cause or the like, nor for any wisdom." Thus they turned the reality of command and prohibition into determinism (jabr), just as they negated causes and wisdom, [p-1915] and negated the power of servants. And they, although they refute the Qadariyya and mention from their contradictions what shows the corruption of the Qadariyya's doctrine, have answered falsehood with falsehood and fought one innovation with another. This is like the Jews refuting the Christians and the Christians refuting the Jews concerning the Messiah, when both doctrines are false. Likewise the confrontation of the Kharijites and the Shi'a concerning Ali is false, and similar examples are many.

End. So memorize this, for it will benefit you in many places.

And His saying, may He be exalted:

The discussion of the words of His saying, Exalted is He:

[12] ﴿And certainly Allah took the covenant of the Children of Israel, and We raised from among them twelve chiefs. And Allah said, "Indeed, I am with you. If you establish prayer, give zakah, believe in My messengers, support them, and lend Allah a goodly loan, I will surely remove your sins from you and admit you to gardens beneath which rivers flow. But whoever of you disbelieves after that has certainly strayed from the sound way."﴾

﴿And certainly Allah took the covenant of the Children of Israel﴾ is a resumed statement, comprising a mention of some of what proceeded from the Children of Israel, of treachery and breaking the covenant, and what that led to of consequences. It is brought to establish the believers upon remembering the favour of Allah Exalted and observing the right of the covenant by which He bound them, and to warn them against breaking it. Or it is to confirm what was mentioned of the intention of the Banu Qurayzah to strike, and to establish it, as has passed in the narration, by clarifying that treachery and betrayal are an old custom for them, inherited from their forefathers. Abu al-Su'ud conveyed this.

al-Razi added: it establishes the obligation of responsibility (taklif) as the way of Allah with those who passed before.

﴿And We raised from among them twelve chiefs﴾: a leader. He was called a naqib (chief, overseer) because he inspects the state of the people and knows the inner reality of their affair. ﴿And Allah said﴾, that is, to them. In the shift to the first person there is the cultivation of awe and the emphasis of what the speech contains of promise: ﴿Indeed, I am with you﴾, that is, with knowledge, power and support. ﴿If you establish prayer, give zakah, and believe in My messengers﴾ (p-1916), that is, those who come to you, ﴿and support them﴾, that is, assist them and aid them with the sword against the enemies, ﴿and lend Allah﴾, that is, by spending in the way of good, ﴿a goodly loan﴾ without reproach or seeking worldly profit, out of showing off and reputation. ﴿I will surely remove﴾, that is, I will surely erase from you ﴿your sins﴾, your sins. ﴿And I will surely admit you to gardens beneath which﴾, that is, flowing through beneath their trees and dwellings, ﴿rivers﴾: rivers of water, milk, wine and honey. ﴿But whoever of you disbelieves after that﴾, that is, after the taking of the covenant and your acknowledgment of it, ﴿has certainly strayed from the sound way﴾, that is, the clear way, which leads to every lofty goal.

The explanation of His words, exalted is He:

[13] ﴿So for their breaking of their covenant We cursed them and made their hearts hard. They distort words from their places and have forgotten a portion of what they were reminded of. And you will not cease to discover treachery from them, except for a few of them. So pardon them and overlook. Indeed, Allah loves the doers of good.﴾

﴿So for their breaking of their covenant﴾ [The *ba'* (bā') is causal (sababiyya), and *ma* (mā) is superfluous (*mazīda*), for emphasis of the speech and its firm establishment in the soul. That is: because of their breaking of their covenant. Or *ma* is indefinite (*nakira*), meaning: for a great thing that proceeded from them, namely their breaking of their firm covenant, the one on which victory, forgiveness, and a great reward were promised.] ﴿We cursed them﴾, i.e., We removed them far from Our mercy. ﴿And made their hearts hard﴾, such that they do not soften to seeing the signs and warnings, nor are they admonished by any admonition, because of their coarseness and hardness, due to the anger of Allah upon them. That hardness and curse remained among their descendants. ﴿They distort words﴾, i.e., the words of Allah in the Torah, by altering their wordings or their meanings, ﴿from their places﴾ where they were sent down.

Ibn Kathir said: That is, their understandings became corrupt, and their handling of the signs of Allah became bad. They interpreted His Book other than as He revealed it, took it to other than its intended meaning, and said about Him what He did not say. We seek refuge in Allah from that. Abu al-Su'ud said: The sentence is a resumptive (*isti'nāf*) clause explaining the degree of hardness of their hearts, for there is no degree greater than that which encourages audacity in altering the speech of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and fabricating against Him. It has also been said that it is a circumstantial clause (*ḥāl*) from the object of *la'annāhum*.

﴿And have forgotten a portion of what they were reminded of﴾, i.e., they abandoned a substantial share of what they were commanded in the Torah, abandoning it as one who forgets something through his lack of concern for it, such that there was no return for them to it. Or it refers to following Muhammad ﷺ.

﴿And you will not cease to discover treachery from them﴾, i.e., treachery (*khā'ina*, as a verbal noun, *khiyāna*). It is in the form of a verbal noun like *lāghiya* and *kādhiba*. Or it means a treacherous group. The meaning is that deceit and treachery are a continuous habit for them and their ancestors, such that they hardly ever abandon it or conceal it. So you will not cease to see that from them.

Mujahid and others said: That refers to their conspiring together to assassinate the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

﴿Except for a few of them﴾, and they are the believers among them. ﴿So pardon them and overlook﴾, i.e., do not punish them.

Ibn Kathir said: This is what necessitates victory and triumph, as Umar said: "You have never treated one who disobeyed Allah concerning you with the like of obeying Allah concerning him." By this, unity and gathering upon the truth are achieved for them, and perhaps Allah will guide them.

Therefore He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, Allah loves the doers of good﴾, meaning by it pardoning those who do wrong, for that is of the category of *ihsān* (excellence in conduct).

Note:

Some of the exegetes said: In this is an indication of the permissibility of taking oaths concerning future matters, and of taking a surety (*kafīl*) for a right that will be carried out in the future. And in His words, exalted is He, ﴿So for their breaking of their covenant﴾ etc., is evidence of the emphasis of the covenant, the ugliness of breaking it, and that it may strip away the subtle divine grace that keeps one far from sins, and it bequeaths forgetfulness. For this reason He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And have forgotten a portion of what they were reminded of﴾. And it is related from Ibn Mas'ud: "A person may forget some knowledge through disobedience." End.

(p-1918) The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:

[14] ﴿And from those who say, "We are Christians," We took their covenant, but they forgot a portion of what they were reminded of. So We caused among them enmity and hatred until the Day of Resurrection. And Allah will inform them about what they used to do.﴾

﴿And from those who say, "We are Christians," We took their covenant﴾ to worship Allah alone, not to associate anything with Him, and to preserve the law (*shir'ah*) of ʿĪsā, upon him be peace. He attributed their naming themselves "Christians" to themselves, rather than saying "and from the Christians," to indicate that in their saying "We are the helpers of Allah" they are far from truthfulness; it is purely their own fabrication, and they have no share in the support of Allah, Exalted is He. Or it is to show the full extent of the evil of their conduct, by making clear the contradiction between their words and their deeds, since their claim to support Allah, Exalted is He, requires their steadfastness in His obedience and their observance of His covenant. This is what Abu al-Su'ud conveyed.

Al-Nasir said in *al-Intisaf*: There remains a subtle point regarding the singling out of this place for attributing the Christian name to their claim. It does not occur in any other place. Do you not see His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And the Jews and the Christians said, "We are the children of Allah and His beloved."﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 18]? The reason for this, and Allah knows best, is that since the aim in this verse was (p-1919) to censure them for breaking the covenant taken from them concerning the support of Allah, Exalted is He, it was fitting for the statement to begin with what indicates that they did not support Allah and did not fulfill what they had pledged regarding support. Their whole affair was merely uttering the claim of support and saying it, without doing it. And Allah knows best.

Al-Shihab al-Khafaji said: What is found in the books of language and history is that the Christians were attributed to the town of *Nasirah* (Nazareth), that is, the town in which the Messiah was conceived and raised. For this reason he, upon him be peace, was called "the Nazarene." He then said: If it were said in the verse that they are upon the religion of Christianity but not upon it, because they did not act according to its requirements and because they contradicted what is in the Gospel (*Injil*) concerning the good tidings of our Prophet ﷺ, that would be closer to the reason for the naming that they mentioned.

﴿but they forgot a portion of what they were reminded of. So We caused﴾ that is, We cast ﴿among them enmity and hatred until the Day of Resurrection﴾ that is, they will be hostile and hateful toward one another until the Hour arrives, according to what their divergent desires and deviant opinions require, which lead to their splitting into mutually opposed sects, some of which curse others and declare others to be unbelievers. ﴿And Allah will inform them﴾ Allah will inform them in the Hereafter ﴿about what they used to do﴾ of opposition, concealment of the truth, enmity, hatred, and forgetting the abundant share of what they were reminded of. This is a severe warning of recompense and punishment.

A subtle point:

Al-Biqa'i, may Allah have mercy on him, in his *Tafsir*, touched here on mentioning the chiefs (*nuqaba'*) of the Children of Israel by name, and that their number matched the number of the chiefs of the Christians, who are the Disciples (*al-Hawariyyun*), just as it matched the number of the chiefs of the Helpers (*al-Ansar*) at the final Pledge of al-'Aqabah, when the Prophet ﷺ took the pledge of the Helpers for war and to protect him when he reached them. He said to them: "Bring out to me twelve chiefs from among you," as Musa had chosen twelve from his people. They brought out twelve chiefs: nine from the Khazraj and three from the Aws. Al-Biqa'i mentioned that the sending of chiefs from the Children of Israel occurred twice. The first was when Allah spoke to Musa in the wilderness of Sinai on the first day of the second month of the year after their exit from the land of Egypt, and this is detailed in the first chapter of the Book of Numbers (*Sifr al-'Adad*). The second time they were sent to spy out the land of Canaan, and this is also detailed in the thirteenth chapter of the Book of Numbers. Al-Biqa'i then mentioned that of the chiefs of the Jews sent to spy out the land, only Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh were faithful, whereas among the chiefs of the Christians one betrayed, namely Judas, as has passed at His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And they did not kill him, nor did they crucify him﴾ [al-Nisa': 157]. As for the chiefs of the Helpers, all of them were faithful and fulfilled their pledge, by the grace of Allah, Exalted is He.

Al-Biqa'i related the names of the chiefs of the three groups and a glimpse of their accounts, so refer to him, and Allah knows best.

Then, after intensifying the rebuke against the two groups of People of the Book for distorting their scriptures and discarding the covenant, Exalted is He addressed them, calling them to the *Hanifiyyah* (the pure monotheistic religion), so that they might be upon a light from their Lord. He said, Exalted is He:

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 5, verse 15:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[15] ﴿O People of the Scripture, there has certainly come to you Our Messenger, making clear to you much of what you used to conceal of the Scripture and pardoning much. There has certainly come to you from Allah a light and a clear Book.﴾

﴿O People of the Scripture, there has certainly come to you Our Messenger, making clear to you much of what you used to conceal of the Scripture﴾ That is: from among the matters concerning his mission (ﷺ), the verse of stoning (al-rajm) in the Torah, and the good news of Jesus concerning him, manifesting the truth. ﴿And pardoning much﴾ That is: of what you conceal, he does not make clear, of what there is no necessity to clarify, sparing you from further disgrace. Or he pardons, so he does not take you to account. In this verse there is an demonstration of his miracle (ﷺ), for he did not read any book nor learn knowledge from anyone, so his informing them of the secrets of what is in their book is information about the unseen, and so it is a miracle. ﴿There has certainly come to you from Allah a light and a clear Book﴾ He means the Qur'an, because it dispels the darkness of polytheism and doubt, and because it makes clear what was hidden from people of the truth. Or because it is manifestly miraculous. Or "light" refers to Muhammad (ﷺ), because he is guided by, just as he was called a lamp (siraj).

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[16] ﴿Through it, Allah guides those who follow His pleasure to the ways of peace, and brings them out of darkness into light by His permission, and guides them to a straight path.﴾

﴿Through it, Allah guides those who follow His pleasure﴾ — i.e., His good pleasure, by believing in Him. ﴿To the ways of peace﴾ — i.e., the paths of safety and salvation from the punishment of Allah. ﴿And brings them out of darkness into light﴾ — i.e., from the darknesses of disbelief and doubts into the light of faith and the decisive proofs. ﴿By His permission﴾ — i.e., by His enabling and His will. ﴿And guides them to a straight path﴾ — which is the true, upright religion in beliefs and deeds, free from excess and deficiency in them. Then he pointed to the excess of some Christians regarding ʿĪsā, and their deficiency regarding the right of Allah, majestic is His glory, so he said:

The discussion concerning the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[17] ﴿Certainly they have disbelieved who say, "Indeed, Allah is the Messiah, the son of Mary." Say, "Then who could prevent Allah at all if He wished to destroy the Messiah, the son of Mary, and his mother and everyone on earth entirely? And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them. He creates what He wills, and Allah is over all things competent."﴾

﴿Certainly they have disbelieved who say, "Indeed, Allah is the Messiah, the son of Mary."﴾ In this verse there are two aspects:

The first: What it implies by way of restriction (ḥaṣr), even though they did not state it explicitly, is attributed to them because it is a necessary consequence of their doctrine, since their belief leads to it.

Al-Rāzī said: Because they say that the hypostasis (uqnūm, a term for a distinct person within the Trinity) of the Word (al-Kalimah) became united (ittaḥada) with ʿĪsā, peace be upon him. The hypostasis of the Word is either an essence (dhāt) or an attribute (ṣifah). If it is an essence, then the essence of Allah, exalted is He, has indwelt in ʿĪsā and become united with ʿĪsā, so ʿĪsā would be the God according to this view. And if we say that the hypostasis is an expression for an attribute, then the transfer of an attribute from one essence to another essence is not rationally conceivable. Then, supposing the hypostasis of knowledge were transferred from the essence of Allah, exalted is He, to ʿĪsā, it would follow that the essence of Allah would be devoid of knowledge, and whoever is not knowing is not a god. Then, in that case, the God would be ʿĪsā, according to their view. Thus it is established that the Christians, even though they do not state this doctrine explicitly, the essential outcome of their position is nothing other than that. End of quotation.

The invalidity of unification (ittiḥād) is known by necessity (al-badāhah).

Al-ʿAllāmah al-ʿUḍud said in (al-Mawqif al-Thānī): The eighth principle: Two things do not unify. This is a necessary judgment, for the difference between two quiddities and two identities is a difference in essence, so its removal is not conceivable. This may be further clarified by saying: If both identities cease to exist, then there is no unification, but rather a third thing arises other than them both. And if one of them ceases to exist, then the non-existent does not unite with the existent. And if both exist, then they are two as they were, so there is also no unification. End of quotation.

The second aspect: By this verse was meant a group who say that the true reality of Allah is the Messiah and nothing else.

Al-Zamakhsharī said: It has been said that among the Christians there were a group who said this. End of quotation.

The Imam al-Shahrastānī said in *al-Milal wa al-Niḥal*, when mentioning the sects of the Christians:

Among them are the Jacobites (al-Yaʿqūbiyyah), the followers of Jacob. They spoke of the three hypostases, as we have mentioned, except that they said: the Word was transformed into flesh and blood, so the God became the Messiah, who manifested himself in his body, rather, he is He. And concerning them the noble Qur'an informed us: ﴿Certainly they have disbelieved who say, "Indeed, Allah is the Messiah, the son of Mary."﴾ Among them (p-1923) is one who said: The Messiah is Allah. And among them is one who said: The divinity (al-lāhūt) appeared through the humanity (al-nāsūt), so the humanity of the Messiah became the locus of manifestation of the Truth. Not by way of the indwelling of a part within it, nor by way of the unification of the Word which is in the status of an attribute, but he became He Himself. This is like saying: The angel appeared in the form of a human, or the devil appeared in the form of an animal… etc.

The Imam al-Māwardī mentioned in *Aʿlām al-Nubuwwah*: The earliest Nestorians said: ʿĪsā is Allah. End of quotation.

The Imam Ibn Isḥāq mentioned in *al-Sīrah*: When the Christians of Najrān came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, they were of Christianity according to the religion of their king, with some disagreement among them. They would say: He is Allah; and they would say: He is the son of Allah; and they would say: He is the third of three, meaning He, exalted is He, and ʿĪsā and Mary; and likewise is the saying of the Christians. Then he said: In all of that which they say, the Qur'an has been revealed. End of quotation.

﴿Say﴾, that is, as a rebuke to them and to make manifest the corruption of their saying: ﴿Then who could prevent Allah at all﴾, that is, who is able to restrain any part of His power, exalted is He: ﴿if He wished to destroy the Messiah, the son of Mary﴾, that is, cause him to die: ﴿and his mother and everyone on earth entirely﴾, that is, let alone their individuals. This was argued as a proof against the corruption of their saying. Its explanation: The Messiah is undoubtedly created, since he was produced from a mother, which is why the mother was mentioned, to draw attention to this. And he is subjugated, and capable of annihilation as well, like all possible beings. And whoever is like this, how can he be a god?

Abū al-Suʿūd said: The generalization of the intention of destruction to all (while the desired goal is achieved by restricting it to the Messiah) is to magnify the matter and to show the complete powerlessness, by explaining that all are under His domination and sovereignty. No one can ward off what He intends for him, let alone ward off what He intends for others. And to indicate that the Messiah is a model like all created beings in being subject to destruction, just as he is a model for them in what has been mentioned of powerlessness and not deserving divinity.

﴿And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them﴾, of creatures and wonders. This is an affirmation of the exclusivity of divinity to Him, exalted is He, immediately after the explanation of its negation from others. ﴿He creates what He wills﴾ is a resumptive clause (jumlah mustaʾnafah) brought to explain some of the rulings of dominion and divinity in a manner that removes the doubt that afflicted them regarding the matter of the Messiah: his birth without a father, the raising of the dead, and the healing of the blind-born and the leper. That is: He creates what He wills of kinds of creation as He wills, with a father or without a father…!

Al-Samarqandī said: He said, ﴿He creates what He wills﴾, because the Christians of Najrān used to say: If ʿĪsā were a human, he would have had a father. So Allah, exalted is He, informed them that He is capable of creating a creature without a father.

﴿And Allah over all things﴾, of creating creatures, and rewarding His allies, and punishing His enemies: ﴿is competent﴾.

**The commentary on His saying, Exalted is He:**

[18] ﴿The Jews and the Christians said, "We are the children of God and His beloved." Say, "Then why does He punish you for your sins? Rather, you are human beings of those whom He has created. He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills. And to God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, and to Him is the return."﴾

﴿The Jews and the Christians said, "We are the children of God and His beloved"﴾ is a report of the false claim made by both groups, and an explanation of its falsehood after the falsehood of what each of them said has been shown. That is: they said, "We stand with God in the same rank as sons stand with fathers, in nearness and honor. And we are His beloved because we are upon His religion."

Ibn Kathir said: They related from their scripture that God said to His servant Israel, "You are My firstborn son." They took this in other than its intended sense and distorted it. Several of their intelligent men who had embraced Islam refuted this, and said: "This term is used among them as an expression of honor and esteem." Likewise, the Christians related from their scripture that Jesus said to them, "I am going to my Father and your Father," meaning my Lord and your Lord. It is well known that they did not claim for themselves the prophethood that they claimed for Jesus, peace be upon him; they only intended by this their closeness to him and their favored standing with him... End of quotation.

Al-Jalal al-Dawwani said in *Sharh 'Aqa'id al-'Adud*: What is related from the Gospel—assuming its authenticity and the absence of distortion—the application of "Father" to Him is in the sense of "origin" (al-mabda'), for the ancients used to call origins "fathers." You know that the ambiguous passages (mutashabihat) in the Qur'an and in other divine books are numerous, and the scholars return them by interpretation to what is known by evidence. So if that were established, it would belong to this category. End of quotation.

Al-Dihlawi said in *al-Fawz al-Kabir*: God, Mighty and Majestic, honored the prophets and their followers in every religious community with the title of "the one brought near" and "the beloved," and He condemned those who deny the religion with the attribute of being "hated." The matter has been discussed with a term common among every people, so it is no wonder that the word "sons" was mentioned in the position of the beloved. The Jews thought that this honor revolved around the name "Jew," "Hebrew," or "Israelite." They did not know that it revolves around the attribute of submission and obedience, and of carrying out what the Truth, glorified is He, intended by sending the prophets, and nothing else. There had become fixed in their minds much of this kind of corrupt interpretation, taken from their fathers and forefathers, and the Qur'an removed these doubts in the most complete manner. End of quotation.

﴿Say, "Then why does He punish you for your sins?"﴾ That is: if you were His sons and His beloved, He would not punish you. But the implication is negated, since He has punished you in this world by killing, captivity, and transformation, and you have acknowledged that He will punish you with the Fire for a number of days.

A subtle point:

One of the shaykhs of the Sufis said to some jurists: "Where do you find in the Qur'an that the beloved does not punish his beloved?" The jurist did not answer him, so the Sufi recited to him this verse: ﴿Say, "Then why does He punish you for your sins?"﴾. What he said is good, and it has a witness in the *Musnad* of Imam Ahmad, where he said: Ibn Abi 'Adiyy narrated to us, (p-1926) from Humayd, from Anas, who said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) passed by a group of his companions, and there was a child in the road. When his mother saw the people, she feared for her child that he would be trampled, so she came running and saying, 'My son! My son!' She ran and took him. The people said, 'O Messenger of God! This woman would never throw her child into the Fire!' He said: The Prophet (ﷺ) quieted them and said, 'No. And God does not throw His beloved into the Fire.'" Ibn Kathir said: Ahmad alone related it. End of quotation.

Al-Samarqandi said: In the verse there is evidence that when God loves His servant, He forgives his sins and does not punish him for his sins. For He, exalted is He, argued against them, saying: "Why then does He punish you, if you were His beloved?" And He said in another verse: ﴿Indeed, God loves those who repent and loves those who purify themselves﴾ [al-Baqarah: 222]. So in it is evidence that He does not punish those who repent for their sins, nor the fighters who fight in His cause: ﴿Indeed, God loves those who fight in His cause in a row, as if they were a structure joined firmly﴾ [al-Saff: 4].

His saying, exalted is He, ﴿Rather, you are human beings﴾ is a conjunction with an implied premise that the speech entails, meaning: you are not as you claim; rather, you are human beings. ﴿of those whom He has created﴾ means: of the same kind as those He created, with no superiority for you over them. ﴿He forgives whom He wills﴾ means: whoever repents from Judaism and Christianity. ﴿and punishes whom He wills﴾ means: whoever dies upon Judaism and Christianity. ﴿And to God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, and to Him is the return﴾ meaning: the place of return, the destination of whoever believes and whoever does not believe. So He will recompense the good-doer for his goodness and the wrongdoer for his wrongdoing.

[p-1927]

**The interpretation of His statement, exalted is He:**

[19] ﴿O People of the Scripture, there has certainly come to you Our Messenger, making clear to you [the truth] after a gap in the messengers, lest you say, "There came not to us any bringer of good tidings or any warner. But there has certainly come to you a bringer of good tidings and a warner. And Allah is over all things competent."﴾

﴿O People of the Scripture, there has certainly come to you Our Messenger, making clear to you﴾, i.e., what you have been commanded and what you have been forbidden. ﴿after a gap in the messengers﴾ is connected to (جاءكم, "has come to you"), meaning: he came at a time of lull in the sending of messengers and a cessation of revelation, since there was no messenger between him and Jesus. The duration of the fatrah (the interval between messengers) between them was five hundred and sixty-nine years.

﴿lest you say, "There came not to us any bringer of good tidings or any warner."﴾ is a causal clause (ta'lil) for the coming of the Messenger with clarification, with an omitted modifier (hadhf al-mudaf, omission of the governed noun). That is: lest you make excuses on the Day of Resurrection and say: "There came not to us any messenger, after the religion had been effaced, who would give us good tidings so that we would desire [it] and act by what would make us happy and so succeed, and who would warn us so that we would fear [it] and abandon what would make us wretched and so be safe." And in that interval the truth had become mixed with falsehood, as we will explain.

﴿But there has certainly come to you a bringer of good tidings and a warner.﴾ is connected to an omitted element that is indicated by the fa' al-fasihah (the "eloquent fa'", i.e., a fa' that signals an implied condition), and it shows that the clause is a reason for it. That is: do not make excuses with "what came to us," for there has come to you a bringer of good tidings, what a bringer of good tidings, and a warner, what a warner.

﴿And Allah is over all things competent.﴾ from sending the messengers, and the reward for those who respond to the messengers, and the punishment for those who do not respond to them.

Al-Biqa'i said: In concluding with the description of power, and following it with a reminder of what they had come to of honour through prophethood and kingship, after they had been in humiliation through servitude and ignorance, [there is] an indication that their denial that a prophet should come from the offspring of Isma'il, peace be upon him, entails their denial of [Allah's] power.

**Note:**

Ibn Kathir said: The interval (fatrah) was between Jesus son of Mary, the last of the prophets of the Children of Israel, and Muhammad, the seal of the prophets, from the children of Adam without qualification [p-1928], as is established in Sahih al-Bukhari, from Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I am the closest of people to the son of Mary; there is no prophet between me and him." This is a refutation of one who claimed that a prophet was sent after Jesus named Khalid ibn Sinan, as related by al-Qudha'i and others. End.

Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar said in Fath al-Bari: It has been cited as evidence, meaning the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, that no one was sent after Jesus except our Prophet (ﷺ). But this is open to scrutiny, because it is reported that the three messengers who were sent to the people of the town whose story is mentioned in Surah Ya Sin were followers of Jesus, and that Jirjis and Khalid ibn Sinan were two prophets who came after Jesus. The answer: this hadith weakens what has been reported about that, for it is sound beyond doubt, while the others are subject to dispute. Or the meaning is: no prophet was sent after Jesus with an independent sharia; rather, whoever was sent after him was sent to confirm the sharia of Jesus. The story of Khalid ibn Sinan was recorded by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak from the hadith of Ibn Abbas, and it has chains which I have gathered in his biography in my book on the Companions. End.

I have mentioned in my book Idah al-Fitrah fi Ahl al-Fatrah, in the eleventh chapter, who among the prophets was in the fatrah according to what has been transmitted. Refer to it.

Ibn Kathir said: The purpose of this verse is that Allah sent Muhammad (ﷺ) at a time of lull in messengers [p-1929], and the obliteration of paths, the alteration of religions, and the multiplication of worshippers of idols, fires, and crosses. So the blessing through him was the most complete of blessings, and the need for him was a general matter, for corruption had spread over all lands, and tyranny and ignorance had appeared among all the servants, except a few who clung to remnants of the religion of the earlier prophets. As Ahmad related from Iyad al-Mujashi'i, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet (ﷺ) once delivered a sermon, and in his sermon he said: "My Lord has commanded me to teach you what you do not know of what He taught me on this day of mine: Every wealth I have given My servants is lawful. Indeed I created My servants all as hanifs (upright in monotheism), but the devils came to them and led them astray from their religion, forbade them what I had made lawful for them, and commanded them to associate with Me what I had not sent down any authority for. Then Allah, mighty and majestic, looked upon the people of the earth and despised them, Arab and non-Arab alike, except for remnants of the People of the Scripture. And He said: 'I have only sent you to test you and to test through you. And I have sent down to you a Book which water cannot wash away; you read it asleep and awake...'" [p-1930] End.

The erudite professor, Shaykh Muhammad Abduh, Mufti of Egypt, said in Risalat al-Tawhid (The Treatise on Monotheism), in the discussion on the message of our Prophet (ﷺ), the following text: It is not our aim in these pages to survey the history of nations in general, and of the Arabs in particular, at the time of the Muhammadan mission, to show how the people of the earth were in dire need of a calamity that would shake the thrones of kings and shatter the foundations of their tyrannical rule, and would lower their gazes, fixed upon the heavens, down to those beneath them of their weak subjects; and to a fire descending from the heaven of truth upon the hides of human souls, to consume what had grown thick upon them of falsehoods deadly to the minds; and to a clear cry that disturbs the heedless, awakens the dazed, and alerts the subjects that they are no further from humanity than the unjust rulers, the misguided guides, and the deceiving leaders; and in sum, that turns them back to a right direction that sets man upon the path which God has laid down: "Indeed, We guided him to the way, either grateful or ungrateful" [76:3], so that by following it he may reach his perfection, and by walking its course arrive at what has been prepared for him in both abodes. But we will borrow from history a word that will be understood by one who looks, with careful and fair attention, at what the historians of that era agreed upon.

[p-1931] The two powers of the world (the Persian state in the East and the Roman state in the West) were in constant strife and conflict; blood was being shed between the two worlds, strength was exhausted, wealth was destroyed, and tyranny was black with enmity. Yet, along with this, arrogance, luxury, extravagance, ostentation, and refinement in pleasures had reached an indescribable extent in the palaces of sultans, emirs, commanders, and heads of religions of every nation, and the greed of this class of nations knew no limit. They increased the taxes and exaggerated in imposing levies until they burdened the backs of the subjects with their demands; they consumed what was in their hands from the fruits of their labour, and the authority of the strong was confined to snatching what was in the hand of the weak. The clever person thought of ways to deceive the heedless, and as a consequence there came over those peoples kinds of poverty, humiliation, submissiveness, fear, and unrest, due to the loss of security for lives and property. The will of the rulers overwhelmed the will of those beneath them, so these became like the shadows of the puppet, moved from behind a curtain, which the onlooker of sound mind takes for real; thus personal independence was lost, and the common subjects came to believe that they had been created only to serve their masters and to provide for their pleasures, as is the case with beasts in relation to their owners. The masters went astray in their beliefs and desires, and their lusts overpowered truth and justice in them. Yet there remained to them of the strength of thought only its worst remnants, for the spark of the divine light that mingles with human natures has not left them, and it may tear the shells that surround the hearts and rend the veils that have been drawn over the minds. So the common people are guided to the path, and the great multitude rises against the small number. Therefore the kings and the leaders did not neglect to create clouds of illusions and to prepare fragments of falsehoods and superstitions, to hurl them into the minds of the common people. Thus the veil thickens, the rust grows, and the light of the natural disposition (fitrah) is suffocated. And what they desire from the vanquished comes to pass for them.

Religion, through the tongues of its leaders, declared itself an enemy of reason and an enemy of everything that reflection produces, except what was an interpretation of a sacred book. And they had in the pagan sources springs that never dry up and a supply that never runs out.

Such was the condition of the peoples in their knowledge, and such was their state in their livelihoods: slaves, humiliated, [p-1932] bewildered in blind ignorance; except for some stray remnants of the past wisdom and earlier laws, which took refuge in some minds, accompanied by hatred of the present and a lack of knowledge of the past. Doubts arose against the foundations of beliefs and their branches, through what had been reversed of the order and inverted of nature, so that filth was seen where purity was expected, greed where contentment was awaited, and debauchery where safety and peace were hoped for. Along with a failure of insight to know the cause, and a hasty turning to the view that the source of all this was religion. Thus confusion took hold of the faculties and led people to a state of chaos in both reason and law together. The doctrines of the libertines and the materialists appeared among many peoples, and this was a calamity for them, over and above the other misfortunes that had befallen them. The Arab nation was tribes at odds with one another in tendencies, subject to desires; each tribe took pride in fighting its sibling, in shedding the blood of its heroes, capturing its women, and plundering its wealth. Greed drove them into the battlefields, and the corruption of beliefs made their evil deeds seem fair to them. The Arabs had reached such a degree of feebleness of reason that they made their idols out of sweets and then worshipped them; when they became hungry, they ate them. And through the decay of morals they reached a weakness in which they killed their daughters to escape the shame of their lives or to avoid the expense of their upkeep. And obscenity reached among them a level at which chastity no longer had any value.

In sum, the bonds of the social order had loosened their knots in every nation, and their ties had been severed among every group.

Was it not, then, among the mercy of Allah toward those peoples that a man from among them should be instructed, to whom His message is revealed, and who is given His care, and who is supplied with such strength that through it he may be able to uncover those calamities which had overshadowed the heads of all nations? Yes, that was so, and the command belongs to Him, before and after. End.

Then he pointed out their negligence regarding the command of Allah revealed through Moses, and their negligence regarding His right, together with his urging them to be grateful to Allah, so that they would hasten to comply with His command. He said:

(p-1933)The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[20] ﴿And when Moses said to his people, "O my people, remember the favor of God upon you when He appointed prophets among you, made you kings, and gave you what He had not given anyone else in the worlds."﴾

﴿And when Moses said to his people, "O my people, remember the favor of God upon you"﴾ That is, the favor which surpasses His favors upon others besides you. So do not neglect His command, since He has not neglected your rights. ﴿when He appointed prophets among you﴾ That is, and they are the most perfect of creatures and the ones who perfect others. He did not send among any nation what He sent among the Children of Israel of prophets. ﴿and made you kings﴾ He means: He made you free, owning yourselves, after you had been enslaved in the hands of the Copts, so God rescued you. He called their rescue "kingship." ﴿and gave you﴾ bestowed upon you ﴿what He had not given anyone else in the worlds﴾ of the kinds of honor with which He singled you out: such as splitting the sea for them, destroying their enemy, making them inherit their wealth, sending down the manna and the quail upon them, bringing forth sweet water from the rock, and shading them with clouds... Therefore the requirement of these blessings is to hasten to carry out the commands of the Benefactor, in gratitude to Him. Then God, exalted is He, informed about Moses's (peace be upon him) exhortation to his people to fight and to enter the Holy House (Bayt al-Maqdis), which the tyrants (jababira) had seized, and that they shrank back and disobeyed his command, so they were punished with wandering (al-tih) for their negligence. Thus He, glorified is He, said, informing about Moses:

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted be He:

[21] ﴿O my people, enter the Holy Land which God has prescribed for you, and do not turn back on your heels, for then you will turn about as losers.﴾

﴿O my people, enter the Holy Land﴾ means the land of Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem), which was holy because of the dwelling there of the prophets who passed before. Then it was defiled by the dwelling of enemies, the tyrannical Canaanites. So He willed to purify it by expelling them and settling His people. ﴿which God has prescribed for you﴾ means which He promised you through the tongue of your father Abraham (ﷺ)(p-١٩٣٤), that it would be an inheritance for his offspring after He had made it his place of emigration (muhajar). ﴿and do not turn back on your heels﴾ means do not draw back retreating on your heels out of fear of the tyrants, out of cowardice and panic. ﴿for then you will turn about as losers﴾ means then you will return defrauded through punishment.

The Discussion Concerning the Interpretation of His, the Exalted, Statement:

[22] ﴿They said, "O Moses, indeed therein is a people of tyrants, and indeed we will never enter it until they leave it. So if they leave it, then indeed we will be entering."﴾

﴿They said, "O Moses, indeed therein is a people of tyrants"﴾ i.e., dominant ones, against whom we have no ability to resist. ﴿And indeed we will never enter it until they leave it﴾ i.e., without any action on our part; for we have no capacity to drive them out of it. ﴿So if they leave it﴾ i.e., by some means with which we have no connection ﴿then indeed we will be entering﴾

**The interpretation of His saying, may He be exalted:**

[23] ﴿Two men from among those who feared (God), upon whom God had bestowed His favour, said: "Enter upon them through the gate, and when you have entered it, you will surely be victorious. And put your trust in God, if you are believers."﴾

﴿Two men﴾: they are Yushaʿ ibn Nun and Kalib ibn Yafna. ﴿From among those who feared﴾: that is, who feared God, the Exalted, rather than the enemy, and who guarded themselves against disobeying His command and prohibition.

The scholar al-Biqaʿi said: That is, from among those in whom fear of the giants was found. Yet despite this, they did not fear, ﴿upon whom God had bestowed His favour﴾: that is, with steadfastness, and with confidence in His promise, the exalted, and with knowledge of the rank of His commands, the exalted. ﴿Enter upon them through the gate﴾: that is, the gate of their city. That is, take them by surprise and prevent them from coming out to the open ground, so that they will not find room for war. ﴿And when you have entered it﴾: that is, the gate of their city, ﴿you will surely be victorious﴾ over them. ﴿And put your trust in God﴾: that is, not in the strength of your own selves. ﴿If you are believers﴾: that is, in the perfection of His power and His promise of victory.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 5, verse 24:

The discussion of His saying, exalted is He:

[24] ﴿They said, "O Moses, indeed we will never enter it as long as they are within it. So go, you and your Lord, and fight. Indeed, we are sitting right here."﴾

﴿They said, "O Moses, indeed we will never enter it as long as they remain﴾ - i.e., the tyrants -: ﴿within it. So go, you and your Lord, and fight. Indeed, we are sitting right here.﴾

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 5, verse 25:

The discussion of His saying, exalted is He:

[25] ﴿He said, "My Lord, I have no control except over myself and my brother, so part us from the defiantly disobedient people."﴾

﴿He said﴾ i.e., Musa, peace be upon him, when he saw from them what he saw of obstinacy, in the manner of pouring out his grief and complaint to Allah, exalted is He: ﴿My Lord, I have no control﴾ i.e., over anyone whom I can compel to fight them, ﴿except over myself and my brother﴾ Harun. Al-Mahayimi said: i.e., and whoever will be a brother to me and agree with me, like Harun, Yusha' and Caleb. ﴿So part us﴾ i.e., judge by that which distinguishes between the righteous and the falsifier, so that You may separate us ﴿from the defiantly disobedient people﴾, i.e., those who depart from your command, and this is in the sense of a supplication against them. Allah answered his supplication and made a separation by causing them to go astray outwardly just as they had gone astray inwardly, as He explained it by His saying, glorified is He:

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 5, verse 26 (part 1 of 2):

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:
[26] ﴿He said, "Then it is forbidden to them for forty years; they will wander bewildered in the land. So do not grieve over the defiant people."﴾

﴿He said, "Then it is forbidden to them"﴾ — that is, the Holy Land — ﴿for forty years; they will wander bewildered in the land﴾ — that is, because of their words and their deeds. They will not enter it or possess it. Whoever uttered this statement or approved of it, the prohibition is a prohibition of restraint, not a prohibition of worship. ﴿For forty years; they will wander bewildered in the land﴾ — that is, they will roam in the wilderness, bewildered in the land, until they all perish. And "at-tih" (bewilderment, the wilderness) is the desert in which its traveler goes astray and loses the way to his destination. ﴿So do not grieve﴾ — that is, do not be sad — ﴿over the defiant people﴾ — that is, those who have departed from the bond of obedience. The scholar al-Biqa'i said: Then, after their destruction, He brought their sons who had been born in the wilderness into it. In this story is the clearest evidence of their breaking of covenants, which the surah was built upon demanding fulfillment of and opened with, and He explicitly stated their taking of it from them in His words: ﴿And God had certainly taken the covenant of the Children of Israel﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 12] and what follows. In this there is consolation for the Prophet (ﷺ) regarding what they do with him, a reminder to him of the blessing upon his people in granting them success, an encouragement for whoever among them obeyed, and a warning for whoever disobeyed. Everyone who uttered that statement or approved of it died during those forty years, including the ten chiefs (nuqaba'). The cloud would shade them from the heat of the sun, and there would be for them a pillar of light at night illuminating them, and other blessings besides this, because the restraint by the wilderness was a discipline for them, not wrath, since they had repented. Then al-Biqa'i — may God have mercy on him — related the account of this story from the Torah that is in their hands, with the burning. We come to its summary, following him, so we say:

It came in the Book of "Numbers" in the thirteenth chapter: that the people of the Children of Israel, when they set out from Hazeroth and camped in the wilderness of Paran, the Lord spoke to Moses to send men to spy out the land of Canaan — one man from each tribe, all of them being leaders of the Children of Israel. Moses sent them and commanded them to look at the land: is it good or bad? And at its people: are they strong or weak? Few or many? And that they should bring back some of its fruit. So they went and spied out the land from the wilderness of Zin to Rehob at the entrance of Hamath, then they returned after forty days. Moses and his people were in the wilderness of Paran at Kadesh; they showed them the fruit of the land, and they recounted to them what they had witnessed of the goodness of the land, that it flows with milk and honey. But because of the might of its people, their strength, and the fortification of their cities, the people of Moses were agitated. Caleb, one of the chiefs, began silencing them before Moses and saying: "Let us go up and inherit the land, for we are able to overcome it." But the rest of the chiefs disagreed with him and said: "We cannot go up against them, for they are stronger than we are." They exaggerated the matter to the Children of Israel and said: "We saw people of great stature, especially the sons of Anak. We were in our own eyes like locusts, and so we were in their eyes." At that, the people of Moses wailed, raised their voices, wept, and said: "Would that we had died in the land of Egypt or in this wilderness! Our women and children shall not become spoil for the tyrants. It would be better for us to return to Egypt." They said: "Let us appoint a leader for ourselves and return to Egypt." When Moses witnessed this from them, he and his brother Aaron fell on their faces before the Israelites. Joshua son of Nun and Caleb, of the chiefs, tore their garments. They spoke to the Children of Israel, saying: "The land through which we passed is good. If our Lord is pleased with us, He will bring us into it. So do not rebel, and do not fear its people, for they will be food for us. The Lord is with us." When the Children of Israel heard the words of Joshua and Caleb, they said: "Let them be stoned with stones." At that time the divine punishment almost befell the Children of Israel, had it not been for Moses' supplication to his Lord to pardon them, lest they become a tale among their enemies, the Egyptians; so God, exalted is He, pardoned them. He informed Moses that his people would not see the land which He had sworn to their fathers, and that they would all die in the wilderness, except Caleb, for due to his good submission he would enter the land, and so would Joshua. God, exalted is He, also informed him that the children of his people who would perish in the wilderness would be shepherds there for forty years, corresponding to the number of days during which the chiefs spied out the land of the Canaanites: a day for a year, its burden, so that they would know His vengeance, exalted is His authority. Then the ten chiefs who had disparaged that land before their people perished by a plague hastened upon them. Then the people of Moses resolved to go up against the Canaanites when Moses informed them of what God, exalted is He, had told him. Moses forbade them and said to them: "There is no victory for you now through the Lord's help; if you do so, the enemy will defeat you and you will fall beneath his sword." But they acted arrogantly and went up to the top of the mountain. The Amalekites and the Canaanites came down upon them and crushed them. Then, after the completion of the forty years, the Holy Land was opened by the hand of Joshua, as explained in his "Book," and God knows best.

Remarks:
First: His words, ﴿forty years﴾, is an adverbial of time related to (they will wander). The possibility that it is an adverbial of (forbidden), as mentioned by more than one scholar, is not valid except with strained interpretation, because of the context of the story which we have explained.

Second: Al-Hakim said: His words, ﴿So do not grieve over the defiant people﴾, indicate that one upon whom God's punishment befalls should not be grieved over, because that is its ruling; rather, he praises God when He destroys one of His enemies.

Third: Ibn Kathir said: Many of the exegetes mention here reports originating from the fabrications of the Children of Israel, about the greatness of the creation of these tyrants, and that among them was Og son of Anak, daughter of Adam, peace be upon him, and that his height was three thousand cubits, and three hundred and thirty-three and a third cubits, the exact calculation. This is something one should be ashamed to mention. Moreover, it contradicts what is established in the two Sahihs: that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "God created Adam, and his height was sixty cubits; then creation continued to diminish until now." Then they mention that this man was a disbeliever, that he was the child of an illicit union, that he refused to board Noah's ship, and that the flood did not reach his knee. This is a lie and a fabrication, for God, exalted is He, mentioned that Noah prayed against the disbelievers on earth, saying: ﴿And Noah said, "My Lord, do not leave upon the earth from among the disbelievers any dweller"﴾ [Nuh: 26], and He said, exalted is He: ﴿So We saved him and those with him in the laden ship﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 119], ﴿Then We drowned the others afterward﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 120], and He said, exalted is He: ﴿There is no protector today from the command of God except He who gives mercy﴾ [Hud: 43]. And if Noah's son, the disbeliever, drowned, how then would Og son of Anak remain, being a disbeliever and an illegitimate child? This is not permissible by reason or by law. Furthermore, the existence of a man called Og son of Anak is questionable. And God knows best.

Fourth: Ibn Kathir said: This story contains a rebuke of the Jews, a statement of their disgraceful conduct and their opposition to God and His Messenger, and their refusal to obey the two of them regarding what they commanded them of jihad. Their souls became weak in persevering against the enemies, disputing with them and fighting them, although among them was the Messenger of God (ﷺ), His interlocutor and His chosen one from among His creation in that era, who promised them victory and triumph over their enemies. This is in addition to what they witnessed of God's action against their enemy, Pharaoh, of punishment, chastisement and drowning for him and his soldiers in the sea while they looked on, so that their eyes might be comforted (and the covenant is not far in time). Then they shrank from fighting the people of a land which, compared to the land of Egypt, does not equal a tenth of a tenth in the number of its people and population. The ugliness of their conduct became evident to the elite and the common, and they were exposed in a disgrace that the night cannot cover nor the train conceal. He also said, may God have mercy on him, before that: How excellent was the answer the Companions — may God be pleased with them — gave on the Day of Badr to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) when he (ﷺ) consulted them about fighting the army that had come to prevent the caravan that was with Abu Sufyan. When the capture of the caravan had escaped them, and the army drew near to them, while they were in a host of between nine hundred and a thousand in equipment, white swords and coats of mail. Abu Bakr — may God be pleased with him — spoke and spoke well, then some of the Companions, from the Emigrants, spoke, while the Messenger of God (ﷺ) kept saying: "Advise me, O Muslims!" He said this only to learn what the Helpers had to say, for they were the majority of people that day. Sa'd ibn Mu'adh said: "It is as if you are alluding to us, O Messenger of God? By Him who sent you with the truth! If you were to lead us through this sea and plunge into it, we would plunge into it with you. Not a single man of us would stay behind, and we do not dislike that you meet our enemy with us tomorrow. We are steadfast in war and truthful in encounter. Perhaps God will show you from us what will comfort your eye. So proceed in God's blessing." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) was delighted by Sa'd's words and was encouraged by them.

Imam Ahmad related from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: "I witnessed from al-Miqdad a stance which, were I to be his companion in it, would be dearer to me than anything else that could be exchanged for it. He came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) while he was supplicating against the polytheists and said: 'By God! O Messenger of God! We will not say as the Children of Israel said to Moses: Go you and your Lord and fight, for we are sitting here. Rather, we will fight on your right, on your left, before you, and behind you.'

I saw the face of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) shine with joy at that, and it pleased him." This was related likewise by al-Bukhari in "al-Maghazi."

Fifth: The Umranis (those who study the building of civilizations) inferred from this verse that among the obstacles to sovereignty is the occurrence of humiliation for a people and their submission to others.

The Wise Ibn Khaldun said in the *Muqaddimat al-Ibar* (*Muqaddimah*), in Chapter 19 under the heading mentioned: Subjugation and submissiveness break the force and intensity of *'asabiyyah* (group solidarity and esprit de corps). Their submission and humiliation are evidence of its loss. They did not become accustomed to humiliation until they were unable to defend themselves, and whoever is unable to defend himself is even more unable to resist or to make demands. This is seen in the Children of Israel when Musa (peace be upon him) called them to the king of al-Sham and told them that God had decreed its kingdom for them. How they failed to do so! They said: "Indeed, there are in it a people of tyrants, and we will never enter it until they leave it." That is, God would remove them from it by some form of His power, not by our *'asabiyyah*, and this would be one of your miracles, O Musa. When he insisted upon them, they persisted and committed disobedience, and said to him: "So go, you and your Lord, and fight, while we sit here." This was only because of what they perceived in themselves of inability to resist and to make demands, as the verse and what is related in its interpretation require. This was due to the character of submission that had taken hold of them, and to the humiliation they had accepted from the Copts for long ages, until their *'asabiyyah* had completely disappeared. [p. 1942] Moreover, they had not believed with true belief in what Musa had told them, that al-Sham was theirs, and that the Amalekites who were in Ariha (Jericho) were their prey, by a decree from God that He had ordained for them. So they desisted from that and failed, relying on what they knew of their own inability to make demands, because of the character of humiliation that had taken hold of them. They also denied what their Prophet had told them about this and what he had commanded them. So God punished them with *al-tih* (wandering), which means they wandered in a barren stretch of land between al-Sham and Egypt for forty years. During that time they did not settle in any inhabited place, did not stay in any city, and did not mix with any people, as the Qur'an relates, because of the severity of the Amalekites in al-Sham and the Copts in Egypt against them, given their inability to resist them, as they claimed. It appears from the context and implication of the verse that the wisdom of this wandering was intended: namely, the death of the generation that had come out from under the grip of humiliation, oppression and weakness, and had adopted its character, and had corrupted its *'asabiyyah*. Thus there arose during that wandering another generation, mighty, that did not know subjugation or oppression and was not subjected to humiliation. Through this, a different *'asabiyyah* arose for them, by which they were empowered to make demands and to prevail. It becomes clear to you from this that forty years is the minimum period in which one generation passes away and another generation grows up. Glory be to the Wise, the All-Knowing. In this is the clearest evidence of the importance of *'asabiyyah*, that it is by it that defense, resistance, protection and making demands are achieved, and that whoever loses it is unable to do all of that.

Then the Most High explained the grim consequence of transgression and envy, in the story of the two sons of Adam from the same father, as an allusion to the Jews, and that if they persisted in their transgression and envy, they would return with the losing description in both worlds. So the Most High said:

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 5, verse 27:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[27] ﴿And recite to them the news of the two sons of Adam, in truth, when they each offered a sacrifice, and it was accepted from one of them but was not accepted from the other. He said, "I will surely kill you." He said, "Allah only accepts from the righteous."﴾

﴿And recite to them﴾ i.e., to these rebellious envious ones among the Jews and their likes, ﴿the news of the two sons of Adam﴾, Habil (Abel) and Qabil (Cain), ﴿in truth﴾, i.e., with truthfulness and accuracy, in agreement with what is in their books. (p-1943) ﴿when they each offered a sacrifice﴾, i.e., that by which one draws near to Allah, the Exalted, of an offering or charity. Habil was a shepherd of sheep, and Qabil tilled the land. Habil offered some of the firstborn of his flock and some of its fattest. Qabil offered some inferior produce of the land's fruit. So it was accepted from one of them, who was Habil, and was not accepted from the other, who was Qabil. Qabil said to Habil: ﴿I will surely kill you﴾ over the acceptance of your offering. ﴿He said, "Allah only accepts from the righteous"﴾, i.e., you were only brought low from your own side, through your soul's stripping off the garment of piety, not from my side. So why would you kill me? And what is wrong with you that you do not reproach your own soul and do not bring it to the fear of Allah, which is the cause of acceptance? He answered him with wise, concise speech comprehensive of meanings. In it is evidence that Allah, the Exalted, accepts no act of worship except from a believing, God-fearing person. How much this rebukes most of those who do deeds!

On the authority of Amir ibn Abdullah: that he wept when death approached him. He was asked: "What makes you weep, when you were such and such?" He said: "I hear Allah saying: ﴿Allah only accepts from the righteous﴾." Thus in al-Kashshaf.

Ibn Abi Hatim related on the authority of Mu'adh ibn Jabal, who said: People will be held in one plain, and a caller will call out: "Where are the God-fearing?" They will stand in a shelter of the Most Merciful, where Allah will not veil Himself from them nor conceal Himself.

I said: Who are the God-fearing? He said: A people who guarded against shirk and the worship of idols and made their worship sincere. They will pass on to Paradise.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 5, verse 28:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[28] ﴿If you stretch your hand toward me to kill me, I shall not stretch my hand toward you to kill you. Indeed, I fear Allah, the Lord of the worlds.﴾

﴿If you stretch﴾, i.e., extend: ﴿your hand toward me to kill me﴾, i.e., unjustly: ﴿I shall not stretch my hand toward you to kill you﴾, i.e., in repelling (the attack): ﴿Indeed, I fear Allah, the Lord of the worlds﴾, i.e., lest I do what you wish to do.

(p-1944) In the "Two Sahihs" (al-Sahihayn), it is related from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "When two Muslims confront each other with their swords, the killer and the killed are in the Fire." They said: "O Messenger of Allah! This is the killer, but what about the killed?" He said: "Indeed, he was eager to kill his companion." Imam Ahmad, Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi related, in the hadith of Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, who said: "I said: 'O Messenger of Allah! What do you think if someone enters my house and stretches his hand to kill me?' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Be like the son of Adam,' and he recited: ﴿If you stretch﴾ to the end of the verse."

(p-1945) Al-Mahayimi said in his tafsir of this verse: That is: "I, although I am not unjust in repelling, fear Allah lest He dislike from me the demolition of His building that gathers (people) so that He may be manifested in it as the Lord of the worlds." End of quote.

This is a subtle Sufi interpretation.

Abu al-Su'ud said: In it is guidance to Qabil toward the fear of Allah, the Exalted, in the most eloquent and emphatic manner, which is not hidden. As if he said: "I fear Him, exalted is He, if I stretch my hand toward you to kill you, that He would punish me, even if that is from me to repel your enmity toward me. So what is your assumption about your own state, while you are the aggressor and the transgressor?" And describing Him, exalted is He, with the lordship of the worlds is an emphasis on the fear. It was said: Habil was stronger than him, but he refrained from killing him and submitted, out of fear of Allah, exalted is He, because killing for repelling was not permissible at that time. It was also said: out of seeking what is best, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Be the servant of Allah who is killed, and do not be the servant of Allah who kills." The explanation by fear of Him, exalted is He, is rejected by this, unless it is claimed that leaving the better course with him is in the position of disobedience in its consequences, in exaggerating purity. End of quote.

The Interpretation of His Words, the Exalted:

[29] ﴿I want you to bear my sin and your sin, and so become among the companions of the Fire. That is the recompense of the wrongdoers.﴾

﴿I want﴾ means: by my submitting to you and my refraining from attacking you. ﴿To bear﴾ means: to return to God, laden ﴿with my sin﴾, that is, the sin of killing me, ﴿and your sin﴾, that is, the sin you committed before killing me, or the sin on account of which your offering was not accepted. ﴿So you become﴾, with both sins, ﴿among the companions of the Fire. That is the recompense of the wrongdoers.﴾

Al-Nasir said in al-Intisaf: As for his wanting his brother's sin and punishment, its meaning is: I do not want to kill you and so be punished. Since there was no escape from wanting one of two things, either his sin, on the assumption that he would defend himself and kill his brother, or his brother's sin, on the assumption that he would submit, and since he did not want the first, he was compelled to the second. Thus he did not want his brother's sin for its own sake; rather he wanted that the sin lies in the defense that leads to killing, and that defense was not lawful at that time, so it followed that he wanted his brother's sin. This is like a person who wishes for martyrdom (shahada). Its meaning is that the unbeliever bears his killing and the sin upon him in that matter, but the one who wishes for it does not intend the unbeliever's sin for its own sake; rather he wants to give up his soul in the way of God, hoping that the unbeliever's sin, through his killing, follows incidentally and by consequence. What shows this is that there is no difference in attaining the rank and virtue of martyrdom between the killer dying in unbelief and the killer being sealed with faith, whereby the sin of the killing, which is why the slain is a martyr, is erased from him. That is, whether the sin remains upon his killer or is erased from him, this neither diminishes nor increases the virtue of his martyrdom. Had the unbeliever's sin through the killing been intended, the wish would differ depending on whether it remained or was erased. This shows that it is a necessary consequence, not an intended aim. And God knows best.

The discourse on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[30] ﴿So his soul permitted him the murder of his brother, and he killed him, and became among the losers.﴾

﴿So his soul permitted him the murder of his brother﴾ That is: his soul made it easy for him and facilitated it for him. The explicit mention of his being his brother serves to magnify the ugliness of what his soul embellished for him, i.e., [the crime of killing] one who, by right, he should have protected from anyone who intended him harm, by bearing [the burden] upon himself. ﴿So he killed him, and became among the losers﴾ in religion, for he became a disbeliever bearing the blood [of his victims] until the Day of Resurrection; and in this world, for he became cast out and hated by creation.

And the compilers [of the six canonical collections], other than Abu Dawud, narrated from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "No soul is killed unjustly except that a share of its blood falls upon the first son of Adam, because he was the first to establish killing." End of quotation.

When he had killed him, he did not know what to do with him, because of the extreme of his bewilderment.

(p-1947) On the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[31] ﴿So Allah sent a crow scratching in the earth to show him how to conceal his brother's corpse. He said, "Woe to me! Am I unable to be like this crow and conceal my brother's corpse?" And he became among the regretful.﴾

﴿So He sent﴾, i.e., He dispatched, ﴿Allah a crow﴾. It came, ﴿scratching﴾, i.e., digging with its beak and feet, delving deep, ﴿in the earth﴾.

Al-Qutaybi said: This is an ellipsis (ikhtisar). Its meaning is: He sent a crow stirring up the soil over a dead body. Al-Suddi transmitted similarly from the Companions that God sent two crows that fought, and one of them killed the other. Then it dug a hole for it and pushed the earth over it.

﴿To show him﴾: the concealed pronoun refers either to God, exalted is He, or to the crow. The apparent reference is to the killer of his brother. ﴿How to conceal﴾, i.e., to hide in the soil, ﴿his brother's corpse﴾, i.e., his dead body. It is called "sawah" (shame) because it is something that offends the one who looks at it. ﴿He said, "O woe is me!"﴾ is an expression of distress and grief; the alif in it replaces the ya' of the first person. Al-waylu and al-waylah mean ruin. ﴿Am I unable﴾, i.e., am I too weak to find the means, ﴿to be like this crow﴾, i.e., the one which is among the most base of animals. The interrogative here expresses astonishment at his failure to be guided to what the crow was guided to. ﴿So I may conceal﴾, i.e., cover, ﴿my brother's corpse﴾. ﴿And he became﴾, i.e., he was, ﴿among the regretful﴾, i.e., regretting his bewilderment at concealing it, since he did not bury him when he killed him. Thus he became more ignorant than the dumb animals, more astray than them, and lower.

In "al-Tanwir" it is said: He was not regretful for his killing.

Abu al-Layth reported from Ibn Abbas: Had his regret been for his killing, the regret would have been a repentance from him.

(p-1948) Notes:

First: The apparent meaning of the verse is that he did not know how to bury the slain, and that he learned that from the crow. There is no barrier to this, since such knowledge may be hidden. Especially since the world was in the early stage of its formation, and he was the first slain, so he was the first dead.

Al-Razi mentioned the possibility that he knew how to bury him. He said: It is far-fetched for a human not to be guided to this degree of action, but when he killed him he left him in the open, treating him with contempt. When he saw the crow burying the other crow, his heart softened, and he did not want to be less compassionate than it. So he concealed him beneath the earth. And God knows best.

Second: The verse indicates that regret, if it is not due to the ugliness of the disobedience, is not repentance. Al-Razi said: He regretted the hardness of his heart and that he was less merciful than the crow. So his regret was for that, not out of fear of God, exalted is He, and therefore that regret did not benefit him.

Third: The verse is a basis for burying the dead.

Fourth: Ibn Jarir said: The people of the Torah assert that when Cain killed his brother Abel, God said to him: "O Cain! Where is your brother Abel?" He said: "I do not know. Am I my brother's keeper?" God said: "The voice of your brother's blood cries out to Me from the earth. Now you are cursed from the earth, which opened its mouth and swallowed your brother's blood from your hand. When you work the earth, it will no longer yield its produce to you, and you will be a trembling wanderer on the earth." End of quotation.
