Fifth: Ibn Jarir reported with his chain from Ali ibn Abi Talib, who said: When the son of Adam killed his brother, Adam wept and said:

Lands have changed, and whoever is upon them; the color of the earth has become dusty and ugly.
Every thing of color and taste has changed, and the radiant brightness of the handsome face has diminished.

Then Adam, upon him be peace, answered:

O father of Abel, both have been killed, and the living has become like the slaughtered dead.
And he came with a fury that had been in him, upon fear, and he came with it crying out.

I say: The first two verses are well known, and many have refuted their attribution to Adam.

Al-Zamakhshari said: It is reported that Adam lamented him with poetry. This is pure falsehood. Poetry is only a forged and ungrammatical composition, and it is established that the prophets, upon them be peace, are protected from poetry. End of quotation.

The commentators said: The word "al-malih" in the aforementioned verse, if it is in the nominative, is an error, because it is an adjective of the genitive "al-wajh"; if it is in the genitive, it is "iqwa'", which is a grave and ugly defect even if frequent. As for the view of one who said, "al-wajh" is the subject of "qalla," and "bashashah" is an accusative of specification with the nunation dropped, treating the pause as continuation, it is more erroneous. It is said that Adam, upon him be peace, lamented him in prose in Syriac. It continued to be transmitted until it reached Ya'rub ibn Qahtan, who was the first to write in Arabic, and he rearranged it, made it Arabic verse.

Al-Khafaji said: There is no doubt that the signs of fabrication are upon it, because of its weakness. But what they found difficult, the iqwa' and the omission of nunation, is not difficult, because similar things occur in the poetry of the pre-Islamic period and of poets. Moreover, it may be explained as an adjective that follows the grammatical position, since "al-wajh" is the agent of the verbal noun, which is "bashashah."

Sixth: The wisdom in specifying the crow is that burying is the crow's habit.

Abu Muslim said: It is the habit of the crow to bury things. A crow came and buried something, and he learned that from it. End of quotation.

The crow is the well-known black bird, and they divided it into kinds. In a hadith, the Prophet (ﷺ) changed the name "ghurab" because of its remoteness (from good), and because it is among the most vile of birds. The Arabs say: "More perceptive than a crow," "more wary than a crow," "more vain than a crow," "more carefree in life than a crow," "blacker than a crow," and "this resembles its father more than a crow resembles a crow." When they describe a land as fertile they say: "It fell into a land whose crows do not fly." They say: "He found the crow's date," because it follows the best dates and picks them out. They say: "More ill-omened than a crow" and "more wicked than a crow." They also say: "The crow of so-and-so has flown," meaning his head has grown white.

"Ghurab ghareb" is an intensive form, as they say "poetry, a poet" and "death, one who dies." Ru'bah said:

So drive away from the birds the crow that is a stranger.

They said: There is nothing on earth that is considered ill-omened except that the crow is more ill-omened than it. Al-Badi' al-Hamadhani has an excellent section describing it. He mentioned it in "al-Mudaf wal-Mansub" and included what the crow is attributed to and what is attributed to the crow. The verses about the crow of separation are numerous; the notebooks are filled with them.

The Imam Abu Abdullah al-Sharif al-Gharnati, qadi of Gharnata, verified in his commentary on "Hazim's Maqsurah" that the crow of separation is in reality the camels that carry them from land to land.

He recited several fragments on this, among them:

They erred, those whom I saw in their ignorance, blaming the crow when all of them cry out.
The fault is only the camels, for they are what scatters their gathering and divides it.
Truly, by the crow's omen the distances draw near, and the swift she-camels scatter the united company.

Ibn al-Minsawi recited from Ibn Abd Rabbih:

The crow screeched, so I said: "The most lying of birds, if the braying of a camel does not confirm it."

Thus in "Taj al-Arus," the commentary on the "Qamus."

And His saying, exalted is He:

(p. 1952)

**The discussion of the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:**

[32] ﴿Because of that, We decreed for the Children of Israel that whoever kills a soul, other than for a soul or for corruption in the land, it is as if he had slain mankind entirely; and whoever saves one, it is as if he had saved mankind entirely. And Our messengers had certainly come to them with clear proofs. Then indeed many of them, after that, are transgressors in the land.﴾

﴿Because of that﴾ means: because of the killing of Qabil (Cain) of Habil (Abel) unjustly. ﴿We decreed﴾ means: We made obligatory and prescribed. ﴿for the Children of Israel﴾. They were singled out for mention because they were the first people to be commanded with this. His words, exalted is He, ﴿that whoever kills a soul other than for a soul﴾ mean: other than for killing a soul that necessitates retaliation (qisas). ﴿or corruption in the land﴾ means: or other than for corruption that necessitates the forfeiture of its blood, such as disbelief together with waging war (hirabah), apostasy, highway robbery (which is mentioned below), and the adultery of a married person. ﴿it is as if he had slain mankind entirely﴾ means: in that he violated the sanctity of blood, instituted killing, and emboldened people toward it. Or: in that the killing of one and the killing of all are equal in drawing down the wrath of God and a great punishment. ﴿And whoever saves one, it is as if he had saved mankind entirely﴾ means: whoever causes that soul's life to remain, by pardoning, by preventing killing, or by rescuing it from some causes of destruction, it is as if he has done this for all mankind.

What is intended by this is the magnification of killing a soul and of preserving it in hearts, as a warning against violating it and as an encouragement to defend it. This was stated by al-Baydawi.

Abu Muslim said regarding the meaning of the verse: whoever kills, it becomes obligatory for the believers to be hostile to him and to be his adversaries, as if he had killed them all, because the Muslims are one hand against whoever is other than them. And whoever saves a life, it becomes obligatory to show allegiance to him, as if he had saved them all. End of quotation.

It was said to al-Hasan al-Basri: "Is this verse for us just as it was for the Children of Israel?" He said: "Yes, by the One besides whom there is no god, it was for them just as it is for us. And He did not make their blood more honourable than our blood."

I say: The rule regarding this is that everything the Qur'an relates from the laws and rulings of earlier peoples, without any indication that they corrupted or fabricated it, is true. Imam al-Shatibi clarified this in his book "al-Muwafaqat", so consult it, for it is important. Al-A'mash related from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayra, who said: "I entered upon Uthman on the day of the siege and said: 'I have come to support you, and the fighting has become intense, O Commander of the Faithful!' He said: 'O Abu Hurayra! Would it please you to kill all the people, with me among them?' I said: 'No! For if you kill one man, it is as if you had killed all the people. So depart, permitted, rewarded, and not burdened with sin.' He said: 'So I departed and did not fight.'"

Imam Ahmad related from Abdullah ibn Amr, who said: "Hamzah ibn Abd al-Muttalib came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and said: 'O Messenger of God! Appoint me to some means by which I may make my living.' The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: 'O Hamzah! Is a soul that you give life to dearer to you, or a soul that you cause to die?' He said: 'Rather, a soul that I give life to.' He said: 'Then keep to your own soul.'"

﴿And Our messengers had certainly come to them﴾, meaning the Children of Israel, ﴿with clear proofs﴾, that is, the manifest verses that state clearly what We prescribed for them, as confirmation of the obligation to observe it and as strengthening the necessity of guarding it. ﴿Then indeed many of them﴾, that is, of the Children of Israel, ﴿after that﴾, that is, after We prescribed it for them and after the coming of the messengers with the signs and the warning that was heard from them, ﴿are transgressors﴾, meaning: in corruption and killing. They do not care about the gravity of that.

Ibn Kathir said: This is a rebuke and reproach to them for committing the forbidden acts after knowing them, just as the Banu Qurayzah, the Banu al-Nadir and others, along with the Banu Qaynuqa, from among the Jews around Medina who used to fight alongside the Aws and the Khazraj whenever wars broke out between them in the Jahiliyyah, and then, when the war laid down its burdens, they would ransom whoever they had taken captive and pay blood-money for whoever they had killed. God, exalted is He, denied this against them in (Surat al-Baqarah) where He says: ﴿And when We took your covenant: You shall not shed your blood, nor expel yourselves from your homes﴾ (Al-Baqarah: 84), and the verses that follow.

Al-Razi said: The purpose of explaining this exaggeration, meaning His words ﴿it is as if he had slain﴾ and the verse, is that the Jews, despite their knowledge of this great exaggeration, proceeded to kill the prophets and messengers, and this indicates the extreme hardness of their hearts and the utmost distance of their remoteness from obedience to God, exalted is He. Since the purpose of mentioning these stories was to console the Messenger (ﷺ) regarding the incident which we have mentioned, in which they resolved to assassinate the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and the chief of his companions, the singling out of the Children of Israel in this story, in this great exaggeration, was appropriate to the speech and confirmed the intended meaning. When God, exalted is He, mentioned the magnification of the sin in killing a soul other than for a soul or corruption, He followed it with an explanation of the corruption that permits killing, with His words, glorified is He:

The discussion concerning His saying, exalted is He:

[33] ﴿Indeed, the penalty for those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger and strive upon the earth [in] corruption is that they be killed or crucified or have their hands and feet cut off from opposite sides, or be exiled from the land. That is a disgrace for them in this world, and for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment.﴾

﴿Indeed, the penalty for﴾, i.e., the recompense for: ﴿those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger﴾, i.e., who oppose them both and disobey their command: ﴿and strive upon the earth [in] corruption﴾, i.e., they act upon the earth with acts of disobedience, and that is killing and taking property unjustly: ﴿that they be killed or crucified or have their hands and feet cut off from opposite sides﴾, i.e., their right hands and their left feet: ﴿or be exiled from the land﴾, i.e., be driven out of it and removed from it. This is banishment from cities, so that they are not allowed to remain in them: ﴿That﴾, i.e., the aforementioned penalty: ﴿is a disgrace﴾, i.e., humiliation and exposure: ﴿for them in this world, and for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment﴾, which is the punishment of the Fire.

The Interpretation of His Words, the Exalted:

[34] ﴿Except those who repent before you gain power over them. So know that Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

﴿Except those who repent﴾, that is, from among the muharibun (those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger, i.e., armed highway robbers and rebels): ﴿before you gain power over them. So know that Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

(p-1955) Concerning this verse there are several issues:

The First: Ibn Jarir, Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that it was revealed concerning the polytheists. Ibn Jarir narrated from Ubayy that it was revealed concerning a group of the People of the Book who broke their covenant with the Prophet ﷺ. It is evident that it is general, covering the polytheists and others who commit these acts. Al-Shaykhan (al-Bukhari and Muslim), the authors of the Sunan, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated, and this wording is his, from Anas ibn Malik: "Some people from 'Urayna came to Madina and found its climate unsuitable. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent them out with the camels of the sadaqa (charity) and commanded them to drink from their urine, and they did so and recovered. Then they apostatized from Islam, killed the herdsman, and drove off the camels. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent after them, and they were brought back. He cut off their hands and feet on opposite sides, branded their eyes with hot iron, and threw them into al-Harra (a lava field). Anas said: 'I saw one of them biting the ground with his mouth from thirst, until they died.' And there was revealed: ﴿Indeed, the punishment of those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger...﴾ [al-Ma'ida: 33], to the end of the verse." In Muslim, from Anas, he said: "The Prophet ﷺ branded the eyes of those only because they had branded the eyes of the herdsmen." In al-Bukhari, Abu Qilaba said: "These people stole, killed, committed disbelief after their faith, and waged war against Allah and His Messenger."

The Second: Some claimed that this verse was revealed as an abrogation (naskh, i.e., the cancellation of an earlier ruling by a later revelation) of the punishment of the 'Uraniyyin mentioned above.

Ibn Jarir said: 'Ali ibn Sahl narrated to us, al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, who said: I discussed with al-Layth ibn Sa'd the branding of their eyes by the Prophet ﷺ and his leaving them until they died, without cauterizing (their wounds). He said: I heard Muhammad ibn 'Ajlan say: "This verse was revealed to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ as a rebuke concerning that, and he was taught the punishment for their like: amputation, killing, and banishment. He did not brand anyone after them." He said: This statement was mentioned to Abu 'Amr, meaning al-Awza'i, and he denied that it was revealed as a rebuke. He said: "Rather, it was the punishment of those specific individuals. Then this verse was revealed concerning the punishment of others who waged war after them, and so the branding was lifted from them."

Ibn Jarir also narrated in the account from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not mutilate anyone before or after that, and he forbade mutilation," and he said: "Do not mutilate anything." The prohibition of mutilation is narrated in the Sahih and the Sunan.

The Third: The majority of scholars used the general wording of this verse to argue that waging war (hirabah) in cities and on the roads is the same. This is based on His saying: ﴿and strive upon the earth in corruption﴾ [al-Ma'ida: 33]. This is the view of Malik, al-Awza'i, al-Layth ibn Sa'd, al-Shafi'i and Ahmad.

Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyya said: "If they brandish weapons within the built-up areas rather than in the open desert to seize property, some have said that they are not muharibun (waging war) but are rather like plunderers, because the one targeted can be reached by help when he calls out to people. But most scholars said: the ruling for those in built-up areas and in the desert is one, and indeed those in built-up areas deserve punishment more than those in the desert, because built-up areas are places of security and tranquility, and because they are places where people support and help one another, so their daring to act there requires greater severity of waging war and overpowering; and because they strip a man of all his wealth in his own house, whereas a traveler generally does not carry with him except part of his wealth. This is the correct view."

Even Malik said concerning one who lures a man, deceives him until he brings him into a house, kills him and takes what he has: "This is hirabah. His blood is for the ruler, not for the victim's guardian, and his pardon has no effect on carrying out the execution."

That was hirabah because killing by trickery is like killing by open force; neither can be guarded against, and indeed the harm of the former may be greater, because one is unaware of it.

It was also said: the muharib is one who openly fights, and this lurer's case is left to the guardian of the blood. But the first view better accords with the foundations of the Shari'a.

The Fourth: The apparent meaning of the verse is that the punishment of those who wage war and spread corruption is one of these types, and the Imam chooses from among them what he sees as beneficial. Ibn Abi Talha narrated from Ibn 'Abbas concerning the verse: "Whoever brandishes weapons in the dome of Islam (i.e., within the Muslim domain) and terrorizes the road, then he is seized and overpowered, the Imam of the Muslims has the choice: if he wishes, he kills him; if he wishes, he crucifies him; and if he wishes, he cuts off his hand and foot." Likewise said Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, Mujahid, 'Ata', (p-1959) al-Hasan al-Basri, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i and al-Dahhak. This was narrated by Ibn Jarir, and something similar was related from Anas.

Ibn Kathir said: "The basis of this view is evident, and there are parallels for the option (takhyir) in the Qur'an, such as His saying concerning the penalty for hunting: ﴿...then a penalty equivalent to what he killed of the livestock, judged by two just men among you, as an offering reaching the Ka'ba, or an expiation: feeding needy people, or the equivalent of that in fasting﴾ [al-Ma'ida: 95], and His saying concerning the expiation for indulgence (shaving during the pilgrimage): ﴿...whoever among you is ill or has an ailment of the head, then a ransom of fasting, or charity, or sacrifice﴾ [al-Baqara: 196], and His saying concerning the expiation for oaths: ﴿...the feeding of ten needy people from the average of what you feed your families, or clothing them, or freeing a slave﴾ [al-Ma'ida: 89]. All of these are optional, so let this verse be likewise." (p-1960) But the majority said: this verse is applied according to circumstances.

al-Shafi'i narrated from Ibrahim ibn Abi Yahya, from Salih, client of al-Tawama, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning highway robbers: "If they kill and take property, they are killed and crucified. If they kill but do not take property, they are killed and not crucified. If they take property but do not kill, their hands and feet are cut off on opposite sides. If they terrorize the road but take no property, they are banished from the land." Ibn Abi Shayba narrated it from 'Abd al-Rahim ibn Sulayman, from Hajjaj, from 'Atiyya, from Ibn 'Abbas, similarly. And similar was narrated from Abu Mijlaz, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, al-Hasan, Qatada, al-Suddi and 'Ata' al-Khurasani. Likewise said more than one of the early generations and the imams. End.

In "al-Nihaya" from the jurisprudence of the Zaydiyya: "The matter of the muharib is referred to the opinion of the Imam. If he sees fit, he kills or crucifies him, because amputation does not remove the harm. If he sees no such need but he is strong, he cuts off his hand and foot on opposite sides. If he lacks strength and judgment, he is beaten and banished. This is the meaning of the choice among these matters: it is left to the Imam's ijtihad (independent legal reasoning), as mentioned." End.

I have seen a valuable section by Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyya concerning the muharibun in his book "al-Siyasa al-Shar'iyya," in which he gave as examples the highway robbers who confront people with weapons on roads and the like to seize their property openly, whether they are Bedouins, Turkmen, Kurds, peasants, corrupt soldiers, rebellious townsmen, or others. Then he cited the narration of al-Shafi'i mentioned above from Ibn 'Abbas, and said:

"This is the view of many scholars, such as al-Shafi'i and Ahmad, may Allah be pleased with them, and it is close to the view of Abu Hanifa, may Allah have mercy on him. Among them are those who say: the Imam may exercise ijtihad regarding them, so he kills whoever he sees killing them as beneficial (p-1961) even if he has not killed, such as a leader obeyed among them, and he amputates whoever he sees amputation as beneficial even if he has not taken property, such as one who is strong and forceful in taking property. Just as among them are those who hold that if they took property, they are killed, amputated and crucified. The first view is the view of the majority. Whoever among the muharibun has killed, the Imam kills him as a prescribed punishment (hadd) that cannot be pardoned in any case, by the consensus of scholars, as Ibn al-Mundhir mentioned. His matter is not left to the heirs of the victim, unlike when a man kills another out of enmity between them, or a dispute, or similar specific causes. In that case, his blood belongs to the victim's heirs: if they wish, they kill him; if they wish, they pardon him; and if they wish, they take the blood money (diya), because he killed for a particular purpose. As for the muharibun, they are killed only for seizing people's property, so their harm is general, like that of thieves. Therefore their killing is a hadd of Allah. This is agreed upon among the jurists, even if the victim was not equal to the killer, such as when the killer is free and the victim a slave, or the killer is Muslim and the victim a dhimmi (protected non-Muslim) or a musta'man (one under safe-conduct). The jurists have differed on whether one is killed for hirabah in such cases. The stronger view is that he is killed for general corruption as a hadd, just as he is amputated if he seizes their property, and just as he is imprisoned for their rights. If the muharibun are a band of robbers, and one of them directly committed the killing while the others were his helpers and supporters, it has been said that only the direct perpetrator is killed. But the majority hold that all of them are killed, even if they were a hundred, and the supporter and the perpetrator are the same. This is what is reported from the Rightly-Guided Caliphs, for 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, killed the 'rabi'a' of the muharibun. The rabi'a is the lookout who sits in a high place and watches for those who come to them."

And because the one who directly commits the killing is only enabled to do so by the strength of the one who backs him and supports him, and when a group is supported by some of its members, until they become a force that can resist, they share in the reward and the punishment, like those who wage jihad. The Prophet ﷺ said: "The blood of the Muslims is equal, the least of them may extend protection on their behalf, and they are a single hand against those who are other than them, and their distant ones are returned to their base" (p-١٩٦٢). This means that if a detachment (sariyyah) split off from the army of the Muslims and seized property, the army shares in what it seized, because the detachment was able to act through the army's backing and strength. However, it is given a special portion (nafl) from it. The Prophet ﷺ used to give a detachment, when they were at the start of their expedition, a quarter after the fifth (khums). When they returned to their homelands and a detachment split off, he gave them a third after the fifth. Likewise, if the army seized booty, the detachment shares in it, because it serves the interest of the army. Just as the Prophet ﷺ allotted a share to Talhah and al-Zubayr on the day of Badr, because he had sent them on a task serving the interest of the army. So the helpers of the group that defends itself and its supporters are part of it, in what benefits them and what burdens them. Likewise, those who fight over falsehood that has no interpretation (ta'wil) behind it, like those who fight out of tribal zealotry (asabiyyah) and the claims of the Jahiliyyah, such as Qays and Yemen and the like, both sides are wrongdoers. As the Prophet ﷺ said: "When two Muslims meet with their swords, the killer and the killed are in the Fire." It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, this is the killer, so what about the killed?" He said: "He intended to kill his companion." (Both al-Bukhari and Muslim) reported it in the two Sahihs.

Each group is liable for what the other destroys of life and property, even if the specific killer is not known, because a single group whose members defend one another is like a single person. As for when they take property only and do not kill, as the Bedouins often do, then from each one his right hand and his left foot are cut off according to the majority of scholars, such as Abu Hanifah, al-Shafi'i, Ahmad and others. This is the meaning of the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿or their hands and feet be cut off from opposite sides﴾ [al-Ma'idah 5:33]. The hand with which he strikes is cut off, and the foot with which he walks is cut off, and his hand and foot are cauterized (tahsim) with boiling oil or the like, so that the blood is stopped and does not flow out and lead to his death. Likewise the hand of the thief is cauterized with oil. This punishment may be more deterrent than killing, for when the Bedouins, the corrupt soldiers and others constantly see among them someone whose hand and foot have been cut off, they recall his crime and refrain. By contrast, killing may be forgotten. And for some proud souls, killing him may have a greater effect than cutting off his hand and foot on opposite sides. So this is a stronger deterrent for him and for those like him. As for when they brandish weapons but kill no one and take no property, then sheathe their weapons or flee and leave the arms behind, they are to be banished (nafy). It has been said that "their banishment" (nafyuhum) means their expulsion (tashrid), so that they are not left to take shelter in any land. It has also been said that it means their imprisonment (habs). And it has been said that it is whatever the imam sees as best of banishment, imprisonment or the like. The legally prescribed killing is striking the neck with a sword or the like, because that is the swiftest (awha, i.e., the quickest) kind of killing. Likewise, Allah prescribed the killing of those whose killing is permitted, among human beings and animals, if one is able to do it in this manner. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Allah has prescribed excellence (ihsan) in everything. So when you kill, kill well, and when you slaughter, slaughter well. Let each of you sharpen his blade and let him spare his slaughtered animal." Reported by Muslim. And he said: "The most gentle of people in killing are the people of faith." As for the crucifixion (salb) mentioned, it is raising them up in a high place so that people may see them and their affair becomes known, and it comes after killing, according to the majority of scholars. Among them are those who said: they are crucified and then killed while on the cross. Some jurists permitted killing them by means other than the sword, to the point that one of them said: they are left on the high place until they die naturally, without being killed.

The Fifth: The conclusion of the verse, I mean His words, the Exalted: ﴿That is a disgrace for them in this world, and for them in the Hereafter there is a great punishment﴾ [al-Ma'idah 5:33], indicates that the hirabah offenders are punished in this world and the Hereafter without exception. The prescribed penalty mentioned does not serve as a purification for them, even if they are Muslims.

(p-١٩٦٤) al-Suyuti said in al-Iklil: Ibn al-Faras said: Its apparent meaning is that the punishment of the muharib is not an expiation (kaffarah) for him, as it is in the rest of the hudud.

And the gnostic al-Sha'rani said in his Mizan: I heard our shaykh, Shaykh al-Islam Zakariyya, may Allah have mercy on him, say: No report has reached us that anyone is taken to account for his sin in both this world and the Hereafter together, except the muharibun, due to His words, the Exalted: ﴿That is a disgrace for them﴾ [al-Ma'idah 5:33], and so on.

Ibn Kathir said: This favours the report that it was revealed concerning the polytheists. As for the people of Islam, in Sahih Muslim, from Ubadah ibn al-Samit, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ took an oath from us, as he took it from the women: that we would not associate anything with Allah, nor steal, nor commit adultery, nor kill our children, nor slander one another. Whoever among you fulfils it, his reward is with Allah, the Exalted. Whoever among you commits a hadd and it is established against him, it is his expiation (kaffarah). Whoever Allah has concealed, his matter is with Allah: if He wills, He punishes him, and if He wills, He forgives him.

The Sixth: His words, the Exalted: ﴿except those who repent before you gain power over them﴾ indicate that the repentance of the muharibun before they are captured removes from them the hadd of the muharibun mentioned in the verse, whether they were polytheists or Muslims. This is related from Ali, Abu Hurayrah, al-Suddi and others. Al-Hadi said: If the muharib repents before he is captured, every consequence of killing or debt falls from him, due to the generality of the verse.

Ibn Kathir said: As for the view of those who say it concerns the people of polytheism, it is clear. That is, if they believe before they are overpowered, all the prescribed hudud fall from them, and they are not held to account for anything of the property or blood they took. Abu Ishaq said: Allah made repentance for the unbelievers remove the hudud that were due upon them in their disbelief, so that this would be an incentive for them to enter Islam. As for Muslim muharibun, if they repent before they are overpowered, it removes from them the obligatory killing, crucifixion and cutting of the leg. Does the cutting of the hand fall away too? On this the scholars have two opinions. The apparent meaning of the verse requires the falling away of all of them, and this is the practice of the Companions (p-١٩٦٥), as Ibn Abi Hatim related from al-Sha'bi, who said: Harithah ibn Badr al-Tamimi, from the people of Basrah, had spread corruption in the land and waged hirabah. He spoke with men of Quraysh, among them al-Hasan ibn Ali, Ibn Abbas and Abdullah ibn Ja'far, and they spoke to Ali on his behalf, but he did not grant him safe-conduct. So he went to Sa'id ibn Qays al-Hamdani, who sheltered him in his house. Then he came to Ali and said: O Commander of the Faithful! What do you say about one who wages war on Allah and His Messenger and strives in the land for corruption? And he recited until he reached: ﴿except those who repent before you gain power over them﴾. Ali said: Write him a safe-conduct. Sa'id ibn Qays said: He was Jariyah ibn Badr. Likewise Ibn Jarir related it through several chains from Mujalid from al-Sha'bi. Harithah ibn Badr said:

Ala abligha Hamdan in innama laqitaha
ala al-nai la yaslam aduwwun ya'ibuha
La'amru abiha inna Hamdana tattaqi al-
Ilaha wa-yaqdi bil-kitabi khatibuha

Ibn Jarir also related, through the chain of Sufyan al-Thawri from al-Suddi and through the chain of Ash'ath, both from Amir al-Sha'bi, who said: A man from Murad came to Abu Musa, who was governor of Kufah in the time of Uthman, may Allah be pleased with him, after he had prayed the obligatory prayer, and said: O Abu Musa! This is the place of one who seeks refuge in you. I am so-and-so son of so-and-so al-Muradi. I waged war on Allah and His Messenger and strove in the land for corruption, and I have repented before you gain power over me. Abu Musa stood up and said: This is so-and-so son of so-and-so. He waged war on Allah and His Messenger and strove in the land for corruption, and he has repented before he was overpowered. So whoever meets him, let him not show him anything but goodness; (if he is truthful, the path of the truthful is his; and if he is lying, his sins will overtake him). The man remained as long as Allah willed, then he went out, and Allah overtook him for his sins and he was killed. Then Ibn Jarir said: Ali related to me, al-Walid ibn Muslim related to us, he said: al-Layth said. And likewise Musa ibn Ishaq al-Madani related to me, and he is the authority with us (p-١٩٦٦), that Ali al-Asadi waged hirabah, terrorised the road, and took blood and property. The leaders and the common people sought him, but he evaded them and could not be captured until he came repentant. This was because he heard a man reciting this verse: ﴿Say: O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah; indeed Allah forgives all sins; indeed He is the Forgiving, the Merciful﴾ [al-Zumar 39:53]. He stopped before him and said: O servant of Allah, repeat its recitation. He repeated it to him. So he sheathed his sword and came repentant, until he reached Madinah at dawn. He washed, then went to the mosque of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and prayed the dawn prayer. Then he sat with Abu Hurayrah among his companions. When it grew light, the people recognised him and rose toward him. Abu Hurayrah said: He has told the truth. Abu Hurayrah took him by the hand until he came to Marwan ibn al-Hakam, during his governorship of Madinah in the time of Mu'awiyah, and said: This is Ali, who came repentant, and you have no way against him, nor any killing. He said: So all of that was set aside. He said: And Ali went out repentant, fighting in the way of Allah by sea. They met the Romans, and they brought his ship close to one of their ships. He stormed onto the Romans' ship, and they were routed from him into their other ship. The ships tilted with them and with him, and they all drowned.

Now, in the tafsir of some Zaydis, transmitted from Zayd, al-Nafs al-Zakiyyah, al-Mu'ayyad billah, Abu Hanifah, Malik and al-Shafi'i, the repentance of the muharib removes the hudud due to Allah, but not the rights of the children of Adam, whether killing or property, due to His words, the Exalted: ﴿And We prescribed for them therein: life for life﴾ [al-Ma'idah 5:45], and His words: ﴿Whoever is killed wrongfully, We have given his heir authority﴾ [al-Isra' 17:33], and His words ﷺ: "The hand is responsible for what it has taken until it returns it," and His words, upon him be prayer and peace: "The property of a Muslim man is not lawful except with the goodwill of his soul." In Sharh al-Ibanah it says: Zayd ibn Ali related, with his chain to the Commander of the Faithful Ali, peace be upon him, that the highway robber, if he repents before he is seized and the imam gains power over him, is liable for the property and is subjected to retaliation (qisas). Then he said: As for the disbeliever, there is no disagreement that his repentance removes from him all the hudud. End.

Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i reported from Ibn Abbas, who said: It was revealed concerning the polytheists; whoever of them repents before he is overpowered, there is no way against him.

This verse does not protect a Muslim man from the hadd if he kills, or spreads corruption in the land, or wages war on Allah and His Messenger.

**(p-1968)** The Discussion on the Interpretation of His, the Exalted's, Statement:

**[35]** ﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah and seek the means of approach to Him, and strive in His cause that you may succeed.﴾

"O you who have believed, fear Allah and seek" — meaning "ask for" — "the means of approach (al-wasilah) to Him," meaning nearness. Thus Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Abu Wa'il, al-Hasan, Zayd, 'Ata', al-Thawri, and others than them explained it. Qatadah said: "Draw near to Him through obedience to Him and acting in what pleases Him." Ibn Zayd recited: ﴿Those whom they call upon seek the means of approach to their Lord﴾ [al-Isra' 17:57]. Ibn Kathir said: "What these imams have said, there is no disagreement among the exegetes (mufassirun) concerning it." In the *al-Qamus* and its commentary: *al-wasilah* and *al-wasilah* (variant form): the rank with the king, the degree, nearness, and connection. Al-Jawhari said: *al-wasilah* is that by which one draws near to another. *Al-tawsil* and *al-tawassul* are the same. It is said: "Wasala ila Allah tawsilan" — he did a deed by which he drew near to Him — like *tawassala*. The phrase *ila* (to) may be connected to *ibtaghu* (seek), and it may be connected to *al-wasilah*.

It was placed before it (i.e., before *wa-jahidu*) for emphasis on it: ﴿and strive in His cause that you may succeed﴾, meaning: by means of striving in His cause. Many verses have explained that striving is with wealth and souls.

**Note:**

What we have mentioned in the explanation of *al-wasilah* is the reliable position. Taqi al-Din Ibn Taymiyyah, may Allah have mercy on him, clarified it in a manner beyond which nothing more is needed, in his *Kitab al-Wasilah*. We have chosen to quote a fragment from it, since the researcher in the science of tafsir has no independence from it.

He, may Allah have mercy on him, said after preliminaries:

The word *al-wasilah* and *al-tawassul* contains generality and ambiguity. Its meanings must be known, and each one with a right must be given his right. So what the Book and the Sunnah have reported of it and its meaning is known. And what the Companions used to say and do, and its meaning. And what the innovators (*al-muhdathun*) introduced in this word and its meaning is known. For much of the confusion of people in this matter is because of the generality and shared usage of words and their meanings, (p-1969) until you find most of them do not know the decisive word (*fasl al-khitab*) in this matter. The word *al-wasilah* is mentioned in the Qur'an in His statement: ﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah and seek the means of approach to Him﴾, and in His statement: ﴿Say: Call upon those you have claimed besides Him; they possess not the removal of harm from you, nor its transfer﴾ [al-Isra' 17:56], and ﴿Those whom they call upon seek the means of approach to their Lord, [competing] as to which of them would be nearest, and they hope for His mercy and fear His punishment. Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is ever feared﴾ [al-Isra' 17:57]. So the *wasilah* which Allah commanded to be sought to Him, and about which He informed that His angels and prophets seek it to Him, is that by which one draws near to Him through obligatory and recommended acts. This *wasilah* which Allah commanded the believers to seek encompasses every obligatory and recommended act, and what is neither obligatory nor recommended does not enter into that, whether it is forbidden, disliked, or permissible. The obligatory and recommended is what the Messenger legislated, commanding it with a command of obligation or recommendation. The root of that is faith in what the Messenger brought. So the sum of the *wasilah* which Allah commanded creation to seek is the tawassul to Him by following what the Messenger brought; there is no means to Allah for anyone except that.

The second: the word *al-wasilah* in the authentic hadiths, such as his statement ﷺ: "Ask Allah for me *al-wasilah*, for it is a degree in Paradise that is not fitting except for one servant of Allah's servants, and I hope that I will be that servant. Whoever asks Allah for me *al-wasilah*, my intercession will be lawful for him on the Day of Resurrection." And his statement: "Whoever says when he hears the call (adhan): O Allah, Lord of this perfect call and established prayer, grant Muhammad *al-wasilah* and *al-fadilah*, and raise him to the praiseworthy station which You have promised him, my intercession will be lawful for him on the Day of Resurrection." So this *wasilah* is specifically for the Prophet ﷺ (p-1970). He commanded us to ask Allah for this *wasilah* for him, and informed us that it is not but for one servant of Allah's servants, and he hopes to be that servant. And this *wasilah* we were commanded to ask for the Messenger ﷺ. He informed us that whoever asks *al-wasilah* for him, intercession becomes due for him on the Day of Resurrection, because the reward is of the same kind as the deed. So when they invoked for the Prophet ﷺ, they deserved that he invoke for them, for intercession is a kind of supplication, as he said: "Whoever sends prayers upon him once, Allah sends prayers upon him ten times for it." As for the tawassul through the Prophet ﷺ and seeking the means through him in the speech of the Companions, they mean seeking the means through his supplication and intercession. The tawassul through him in the usage of many later scholars is meant as swearing by him and asking through him, as they swear by others of the prophets and righteous, and those they believe to be righteous. Then the word *tawassul* through him is used with two correct meanings by the agreement of the Muslims, and a third meaning is used which the Sunnah did not report. As for the two first meanings, which are correct by the agreement of the scholars: one of them is the root of faith and Islam, which is the tawassul through faith in him and obedience to him. The second is his supplication and intercession, as previously mentioned. These two are permissible by the consensus of the Muslims. From this is the statement of Umar ibn al-Khattab: "O Allah, when we were afflicted by drought, we used to seek the means to You through our Prophet, and You would give us rain. And now we seek the means to You through the uncle of our Prophet, so give us rain." That is, through his supplication and intercession. And His statement, the Exalted: ﴿and seek the means of approach to Him﴾, meaning: nearness to Him through obedience to Him. The obedience to His Messenger is obedience to Him; He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed Allah﴾ [al-Nisa' 4:80]. So this first tawassul is the root of the religion, and no one among the Muslims denies it. As for tawassul through his supplication and intercession, as Umar said, it is a tawassul through his supplication, not through his person. For this reason they turned away from seeking the means through him to seeking the means through his uncle al-'Abbas (p-1971), and if the tawassul had been through his person, this would have been more fitting than through al-'Abbas. So when they turned away from seeking the means through him to seeking the means through al-'Abbas, it is known that what was done during his life became impossible with his death. Unlike the tawassul which is faith in him and obedience to him, which is always legislated.

So the word *tawassul* is used with three meanings:

The first: tawassul through his obedience. This is an obligation without which faith is not complete.

The second: tawassul through his supplication and intercession. This existed during his life, and on the Day of Resurrection they will seek the means through his intercession.

The third: tawassul through him in the sense of swearing by Allah through his person and asking through his person. This is what the Companions did not do in seeking rain or the like, neither during his life nor after his death, neither at his grave nor elsewhere, and this is not known in any of the well-known supplications among them. What is transmitted of that is only in weak hadiths, both raised (*marfu'*) and stopped (*mawquf*), or from someone whose statement is not a proof. This is what Abu Hanifah and his companions said is not permissible, and they forbade it, saying: "One should not ask by a created being, and no one should say: I ask You by the right of Your prophets." Abu al-Husayn al-Quduri said in his large book on jurisprudence called *Sharh al-Karkhi*, in the chapter on what is disliked: Many of the companions of Abu Hanifah have mentioned this. Bishr ibn al-Walid said: Abu Yusuf narrated to us, saying: Abu Hanifah said: "It is not fitting for anyone to supplicate except by Him. And I dislike that one says: by the foundations of the honor of Your throne, or by the right of Your creation." This is also the statement of Abu Yusuf. Abu Yusuf said: "By the foundation of the honor of His throne is Allah Himself, so I do not dislike this. But I dislike that one says: by the right of so-and-so, or by the right of Your prophets and messengers, and by the right of the Sacred House and the Sacred Monument." Al-Quduri said: "Asking by His creation is not permissible, because it is an obligation of the creation upon the Creator, so it is not permissible by consensus."

What Abu Hanifah and his companions said, that Allah is not asked by a created being, has two meanings. One of them agrees with the rest of the imams who forbid anyone to swear by a created being. For if it is forbidden to swear by a created being upon a created being, then it is more fitting and more proper that it be forbidden to swear upon the Creator by a created being. This is unlike (p-1972) His, glory be to Him, swearing by His creatures, such as: ﴿By the night when it covers﴾ [al-Layl 92:1], ﴿By the day when it appears﴾ [al-Layl 92:2], ﴿By the sun and its brightness﴾ [al-Shams 91:1], ﴿By those who drag out with violence﴾ [al-Nazi'at 79:1], ﴿By those who line up in rows﴾ [al-Saffat 37:1]. For His swearing by His creatures includes a mention of His signs which indicate His power, wisdom, and oneness, so that His swearing is fitting with it. Unlike the creature, for swearing by creatures is an association with their Creator. As in the *Sunan* from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "Whoever swears by other than Allah has associated (a partner with Allah)." Al-Tirmidhi and others authenticated it. In another wording: "He has disbelieved." Al-Hakim authenticated it. And it is established from him in the two *Sahihs* that he said: "Whoever is swearing, let him swear by Allah." And he said: "Do not swear by your fathers, for Allah forbids you to swear by your fathers." And in the two *Sahihs* from him that he said (p-1973): "Whoever swears by al-Lat and al-'Uzza, let him say: There is no god but Allah." The Muslims agree that whoever swears by respected created things, or by what he believes to be sacred, such as the Throne, the Footstool, the Ka'bah, the Sacred Mosque, the Furthest Mosque, the Mosque of the Prophet ﷺ, the angels, the righteous, the kings, the swords of the mujahidin, the dust of the prophets and righteous, the trousers of chivalry (*futuwwah*), and other such things, his oath is not binding, and there is no expiation for breaking it. Swearing by created things is forbidden according to the majority, and it is the position of Abu Hanifah, and one of the two opinions in the school of al-Shafi'i and Ahmad. He (the author) has also reported the consensus of the Companions upon that. End.

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[36] ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve, even if they had all that is in the earth, and the like of it with it, to ransom themselves therewith from the punishment of the Day of Resurrection, it would not be accepted from them. And for them is a painful punishment.﴾

﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve, if they had what is in the earth﴾

of wealth and other things, ﴿all of it, and the like of it with it, to ransom themselves therewith﴾, i.e., to redeem their souls with it, ﴿from the punishment of the Day of Resurrection, it would not be accepted from them. And for them is a painful punishment.﴾ This is a figurative expression for the inevitability of punishment for them, and that there is no way for them to be saved from it in any manner.

Al-Bukhari narrated from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "A disbeliever will be brought on the Day of Resurrection, and it will be said to him: 'Tell me, if you had the whole earth filled with gold, would you ransom yourself with it?' He will say: 'Yes.' It will be said to him: 'You were asked for something much easier than that: that you not associate anything with Me.' Then he will be ordered to the Fire." Muslim and others narrated it with similar wording.

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[37] ﴿They wish to come out of the Fire, but they will not be able to come out of it, and theirs is a lasting punishment.﴾

﴿They wish to come out of the Fire, but they will not be able to come out of it, and theirs is a lasting punishment﴾: a constant punishment that does not cease. This is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Every time they wish to come out of it, they will be returned to it﴾ [al-Sajdah: 20], and the verse continues.

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Yazid ibn Suhayb al-Faqir, from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "A people will come out of the Fire and enter Paradise." He said: I said to Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, "Does Allah not say: ﴿They wish to come out of the Fire, but they will not be able to come out of it﴾?" He said: "Recite the beginning of the verse: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve, even if they had all that is on the earth and the like of it with it, to ransom themselves thereby﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 36], to the end of the verse. Those are the ones who disbelieved."

Imam Ahmad and Muslim also narrated this hadith by another route, from Yazid al-Faqir, from Jabir, and this one is more detailed in its context.

Ibn Abi Hatim added: Jabir said: "Do you not read the Qur'an?" I said: "Yes, indeed. I have memorised it." He said: "Did Allah not say: ﴿And from the night, pray with it as a supererogatory act for you; perhaps your Lord will raise you to a praiseworthy station﴾ [al-Isra': 79]? That is that station: indeed Allah, exalted is He, detains some people in the Fire for their sins for as long as He wills, not speaking to them; then when He wills to bring them out, He brings them out."

When He, exalted is He, made obligatory in the preceding verse the cutting off of hands and feet for taking property by way of waging war, He made clear that taking property by way of theft also necessitates the cutting off of hands and feet, so He, glorified is He, said:

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 5, verse 38 (part 1 of 2):

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:
[38] ﴿As for the thief, male or female, cut off their hands as a recompense for what they committed, a deterrent punishment from Allah. And Allah is Almighty, Wise.﴾
﴿The thief (al-sariq)﴾ i.e., from among the men; ﴿and the thief (al-sariqah)﴾ i.e., from among the women; ﴿cut off their hands﴾ meaning the right hand of each of them. The place of cutting is the wrist, as the Sunnah has clarified. ﴿As a recompense for what they committed﴾ i.e., cutting off the instrument by which they earned. ﴿A deterrent punishment﴾ i.e., a penalty; ﴿from Allah﴾ i.e., for the act of theft which He has forbidden, from Him, exalted is He, not in return for the destruction of property, for that is other than theft. Therefore it does not lapse by the pardon of the owner, unlike pardoning concerning the property. Nor is consideration given in it to the honour of the thief, because He, exalted is He, prevails over His affair, executing it as He wills, as He said: ﴿And Allah is Almighty﴾ i.e., so He does not heed, along with His might which necessitates obedience to His command, any might other than His: ﴿Wise﴾ in His legislation, so that the order of the world's system would be disrupted by opposing His command, since in it there is general benefit for the creatures.

(p-1977) Regarding the verse there are several issues:

The first: Abu al-Su'ud said: Since theft was known among women as among men, He explicitly mentioned the female thief as well, although the established custom in the Book and the Sunnah is to include women within the rulings revealed concerning men by way of implication, for greater attention to clarification and emphasis in deterrence. End of quote.

And since theft was predominantly committed by men, owing to their strength, He began with the male thief. Just as adultery was predominantly committed by women, owing to the intensity of their desire, He said in the verse on adultery: ﴿The adulteress and the adulterer﴾ [al-Nur: 2].

The second: Ibn Kathir said: al-Thawri narrated with his chain to Ibn Mas'ud that he used to recite it: "And the thief, male and female, cut off their right hands." This is an irregular recitation (qira'ah shadhdhah). The ruling was in agreement with it according to all the scholars, not on account of it, but it is derived from another proof. Cutting was practised in the Jahiliyyah and was confirmed in Islam, and further conditions were added, as we shall mention, Allah willing. Likewise the qasamah, the diyah, the qirad and other things which the Law confirmed in their existing form, with additions that complete the public interests. It is said that the first to cut hands in the Jahiliyyah were the Quraysh, who cut off a man called (Duwayk), a client of Banu Malih ibn 'Amr of Khuza'ah, who had stolen the treasure of the Ka'bah. It is said that a people stole it and placed it with him.

The third: Some jurists of the Zahiriyyah school held that whenever a thief steals anything, his hand is cut off for it, whether it is little or much, on account of the generality of this verse: ﴿As for the thief, male or female, cut off their hands﴾. They did not consider a minimum value (nisab) or a protected place (hirz), but acted merely upon the act of theft.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Najdah al-Hanafi who said: I asked Ibn 'Abbas about His saying: ﴿As for the thief, male or female, cut off their hands﴾, is it specific or general? He said: Rather, it is general. This may indicate that he agreed with those who held this view, and it may indicate otherwise; Allah knows best.

(p-1978) They relied on what is established in the two Sahihs from Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "May Allah curse the thief who steals an egg and his hand is cut off, and steals a rope and his hand is cut off."

As for the majority, they took the nisab into account, although disagreement arose among them concerning its amount.

According to Imam Malik, the nisab is three dirhams of minted pure silver. Whenever one steals it, or something whose value reaches it or exceeds it, cutting becomes obligatory. He argued for this with what he narrated from Nafi' from Ibn 'Umar: "that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ cut off (a hand) for a shield whose price was three dirhams." It is recorded by both in the two Sahihs. Malik, may Allah have mercy on him, said: 'Uthman, may Allah be pleased with him, also cut off a hand for a citron valued at three dirhams. And this is the most beloved of what I have heard on this matter.

The companions of Malik said: Such an action becomes well known and is not denied; from such a thing the tacit consensus (ijma' sukuti) is derived. And in it is evidence for cutting in the case of fruits, contrary to the Hanafis; and for the consideration of three dirhams, contrary to their view that ten dirhams are necessary; and contrary to the Shafi'is in regard to the consideration of a quarter dinar. Allah knows best.

Al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, held that the criterion for cutting off the thief's hand is a quarter dinar, or what equals it in currency or goods, or more. The proof for this is what the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim) narrated through al-Zuhri from 'Amrah from 'A'ishah (p-1979) , may Allah be pleased with her: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The hand of the thief is cut off for a quarter dinar or more." Also in Muslim from her: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The hand of the thief is not cut off except for a quarter dinar or more." The Shafi'is said: This hadith is decisive on the matter, and explicit regarding the consideration of a quarter dinar and nothing other than it. They said: The hadith of the price of the shield, even if it was three dirhams, does not contradict this, because at that time the dinar was equal to twelve dirhams, so three dirhams were the price of a quarter dinar, and thus reconciliation is possible by this means. This view is narrated from 'Umar, 'Uthman and 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with them. It is also the view of 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz, al-Layth, al-Awza'i, Ishaq (in one narration from him), Abu Thawr and Dawud al-Zahiri, may Allah have mercy on them.

Imam Ahmad and Ishaq (in one narration) held that each of the quarter dinar and the three dirhams is a legal measure. Whoever steals one of these two, or what equals it, has his hand cut off, acting upon the hadith of Ibn 'Umar and the hadith of 'A'ishah. In a wording recorded by Imam Ahmad from 'A'ishah it occurs: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Cut off (a hand) for a quarter dinar, and do not cut off for what is less than that." At that time a quarter dinar was three dirhams, and the dinar was twelve dirhams. In a wording of al-Nasa'i: "The hand of the thief is not cut off for less than the price of a shield." It was said to 'A'ishah: What is the price of a shield? She said: A quarter dinar. All these are texts indicating that ten dirhams is not a condition. Allah knows best.

As for Imam Abu Hanifah and his companions, and likewise Sufyan al-Thawri, they held that the nisab is ten minted dirhams that are not adulterated. They argued that the price of the shield for which the thief was cut off in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was ten dirhams, and Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated: Ibn Numayr and 'Abd al-A'la related to us from Muhammad ibn Ishaq from 'Amr ibn Shu'ayb from his father from his grandfather who said: (p-1980) The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The hand of the thief is not cut off for less than the price of a shield." And the price of a shield was ten dirhams. They said: Here Ibn 'Abbas and 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr have differed from Ibn 'Umar regarding the price of the shield. So caution lies in taking the higher amount, because prescribed penalties are averted by doubts.

Some of the early scholars (salaf) held that the hand of the thief is cut off for ten dirhams, or a dinar, or whatever reaches the value of either of them. This is related from 'Ali, Ibn Mas'ud, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i and Abu Ja'far al-Baqir, may Allah the Exalted have mercy on them.

Some of the early scholars said: Five is not cut except for five, i.e., five dinars or fifty dirhams. This is related from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, may Allah have mercy on him.

The majority have answered what the Zahiris relied upon from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah: "He steals an egg and his hand is cut off, and steals a rope and his hand is cut off," with several answers:
One of them: it is abrogated by the hadith of 'A'ishah. But there is scrutiny in this, since the date of the two must be established.
The second: it is interpreted as referring to an iron helmet (bayd al-hadid) and the rope of ships. This was said by al-A'mash, as related by al-Bukhari and others from him.
The third: this is a means of gradual progression in theft from little to much, up to the point where the hand is cut off. It is possible that this was stated as a report about what was the case in the Jahiliyyah, when they cut off hands for much and little alike. Thus the thief who gives his precious hand for contemptible things is cursed.

They mentioned that Abu al-'Ala' al-Ma'arri, when he came to Baghdad, became famous for raising an objection against the jurists for making the nisab of theft a quarter dinar, saying in verse:
"A hand which was valued at five hundred gold coins as blood-money, why was it cut off for a quarter dinar?"

(p-1981) People answered him on this matter. The response of the judge 'Abd al-Wahhab al-Maliki, may Allah have mercy on him, was that he said: When it was a trust, it was precious; when it betrayed, it was debased. Others said: This is part of the completeness of wisdom and benefit and the secrets of the great Shari'ah. In the chapter of injuries, it was fitting that the value of the hand be magnified to five hundred dinars, lest it be harmed. In the chapter of theft, it was fitting that the amount for which the hand is cut be a quarter dinar, lest people hasten to steal property. This is precisely wisdom in the sight of people of understanding. For this reason He said: ﴿A recompense for what they committed, a deterrent punishment from Allah, and Allah is Almighty, Wise﴾, i.e., a requital for their evil deed in taking people's property by their hands, so it was fitting that what they used for that be cut off. Thus in the tafsir of Ibn Kathir.

Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, may his secret be sanctified, said in his book "al-Siyasah al-Shar'iyyah": As for the thief, it is obligatory to cut off his right hand by the Book, the Sunnah and the consensus. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿The thief, male and female﴾ the verse... It is not permissible, once the penalty has been established against him by evidence or confession, to delay it, neither by imprisonment, nor by property with which he ransoms himself, nor otherwise. Rather his hand is cut off in the sacred times and other times. For the execution of the prescribed penalties is an act of worship like jihad in the way of Allah. It should be understood that the execution of the penalty is a mercy from Allah to His servants. Therefore the ruler should be firm in executing the penalty, not taken by compassion in the religion of Allah so that he suspends it, and his intention should be the mercy of creation by restraining people from wrongdoing, not the satisfaction of his anger or the desire for dominance over creatures. Rather he is like a father who disciplines his child. For if he refrained from disciplining his child, as the mother conceals it out of tenderness and compassion, the child would be corrupted. He disciplines him out of mercy and for his reform, while he himself loves and prefers that he never need discipline. He is like the physician who gives the patient a bitter medicine, and like cutting off a decayed limb, cupping, bloodletting by lancing veins, and the like. Indeed, he is like a person who drinks a bitter medicine and bears the hardship he imposes upon himself in order to attain comfort. Thus were the penalties legislated. And so should be the intention of the ruler in executing them. For whoever intends the welfare of the subjects and the prevention of wrongdoing, by bringing benefit to them and removing harm from them, seeking thereby the face of Allah the Exalted and obedience to His command (p-1982), Allah softens hearts toward him and facilitates for him the causes of good, and a light punishment suffices him. The one punished may even be content when the penalty is executed upon him. But if his aim is to dominate over them and display his might so that they give him something or surrender to him wealth as he wishes, his purpose is reversed against him.

It is related that 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz, may Allah have mercy on him, before he assumed the caliphate, was deputy for al-Walid ibn 'Abd al-Malik over the city of the Prophet ﷺ, and he had governed them with good governance. Then al-Hajjaj came from Iraq, having inflicted on them the worst torment, and he asked the people of Medina about 'Umar: "What is his awe among you?" They said: "We cannot look at him out of awe!" He said: "What is your love for him?" They said: "He is dearer to us than our families!" He said: "What is his discipline?" They said: "Between three and ten lashes..." He said: "This is his awe, this is his love, and this is his discipline! This is a command from heaven."

When a hand is cut off, the stump is cauterized, and it is recommended that it be hung around the thief's neck. If he steals a second time, his left foot is cut off. If he steals a third or fourth time, there are two opinions among the Companions and the scholars after them:
One of them: his four limbs are cut off for the third and fourth offences. This is the view of Abu Bakr, the view of al-Shafi'i, may Allah be pleased with him, the Kufans, and Ahmad in one of the two narrations.

"The second [view]: that he is imprisoned. This is the view of ʿAlī (may Allah be pleased with him), of the Kufans, and of Aḥmad in one of his two narrations. The remaining topics concerning theft are established in the books of Sunnah.

The fourth [point]: The majority (al-Jumhūr) read al-sāriqu wa-l-sāriqatu (the thief, male and female) with a nominative ending (rafʿ), as a subject (mubtadaʾ), with the predicate omitted. Its estimated form is: "And in what is recited to you" or "what is enjoined upon you" — al-sāriqu wa-l-sāriqatu, meaning their ruling. Or the predicate is the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿fa-q-ṭaʿū aydiyahumā﴾ ("then cut off their hands"), and the fāʾ (fa) is there because the subject contains the meaning of a conditional (sharṭ), since the sense is: "he who steals and she who steals." ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read it with the accusative (naṣb), and Sībawayh preferred it over the nominative reading, because a construction (inshāʾ) does not occur as a predicate except with an interpretation (taʾwīl) and an implied element (iḍmār); this is what is famously attributed to Sībawayh.

Al-Nāṣir said in al-Intiṣāf: "What is established from the various readings is that the common readers never agree on deviating from the more eloquent form."

It is fitting for the Qur'an to follow the most eloquent form and not to be devoid of the most eloquent, and of what the speech of the Arabs includes, which no one has reached the peak of its eloquence or grasped its edges. Sībawayh would exclude from the belief of the Qur'an's readers that it deviates from the most eloquent, or that it includes an anomalous reading that could not be counted as part of the Qur'an. We shall cite the passage from Sībawayh's words on this verse so that its hearer may see Sībawayh's innocence from the burden of this transmission. Sībawayh said in the chapter heading "Chapter on the Command and the Prohibition," after mentioning the positions in which the accusative is preferred: "Its summary is that whenever the noun is built upon the imperative verb, that is the position where the accusative is preferred." Then he said, as if clarifying the distinction of this verse from those in which he preferred the accusative: "As for His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿wa-l-sāriqu wa-l-sāriqatu﴾ (the verse) and His words: ﴿al-zāniyatu wa-l-zānī fa-jlidū﴾ [al-Nūr: 2], this is not built upon a verb, but it comes in the pattern of His words: ﴿mathalu l-jannati llatī wuʿida l-muttaqūn﴾ [al-Raʿd: 35]," then he said afterward: "in it is such and such." Sībawayh intends by this to distinguish these verses from the positions in which he explained the preference for the accusative. He justified the distinction by saying that wherever the accusative is preferred, the noun in the sentence is built upon the verb, whereas in these verses it is not built upon it, so the accusative is not required in them.

His speech resumes: "The example was given only for the narration he mentions after it, so he mentioned reports and stories. It is as if he said: 'Among the stories is the example of Paradise.' So it is carried upon this implied element. And Allah knows best." And likewise: (p-1984) al-zāniyatu wa-l-zānī. When He, may His praise be exalted, said: ﴿a sūratun anzalnāhā wa-faraḍnāhā﴾ [al-Nūr: 1], He said among the obligations: "al-zāniyatu wa-l-zānī," and then came: "fa-jlidū" after the nominative had passed in them. Sībawayh intends: the noun was not built upon the verb mentioned afterward, but was built upon an earlier omitted element, and the verb came as an interruption.

His speech resumes: "As it came: 'wa-qā'ilatin Khawlāna fa-nkiḥ fatātahum' (And a woman of Khawlān said: marry her young woman). So the verb came after the pronoun had governed it. Likewise: wa-l-sāriqu wa-l-sāriqatu, and fīmā furiḍa ʿalaykum al-sāriqatu wa-l-sāriqu. These nouns entered after stories and reports." Some people read: wa-l-sāriqa wa-l-sāriqata with the accusative, and in Arabic it has the strength I have mentioned to you, but the common readers refused anything except the nominative.

Sībawayh intends that in the accusative reading the noun is built upon the verb without depending on an earlier element, so the accusative is strong in comparison with the nominative, in the case where the noun is built upon the verb and not upon an earlier element. He does not mean that it is strong in comparison with the nominative in the case where the noun depends upon the omitted earlier element; for he has made clear that this removes it from the category in which the accusative is preferred. How, then, could his preference of it over the nominative be understood, when the category differs between the two readings? Preference only occurs after equality within the same category. So the accusative is preferable to the nominative where the noun is built upon the verb, while the nominative is required (I do not say preferable) where the noun is built upon a preceding statement.

Then Sībawayh verified this estimated element by saying that the speech occurs after stories and reports. Had it been as al-Zamakhsharī supposed, Sībawayh would not have needed an estimate; rather he would have put it in the nominative as a subject, with the command as its predicate. So the summary according to this is: the accusative has one mode, namely building the noun upon the imperative verb. The nominative has two modes: one of them is weak, namely beginning (ibtidāʾ) and building the speech upon the verb; the other is strong and fully established, like the mode of the accusative, namely its nominative as the predicate of an omitted subject indicated by the context. Wherever two modes of the nominative conflict for us, (p-1985) one strong and one weak, it is necessary to carry the reading upon the strong one, as Sībawayh, may Allah be pleased with him, analyzed it. And Allah knows best. End of quotation.

And His words, Exalted is He:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[39] ﴿But whoever repents after his wrongdoing and makes amends, indeed Allah will turn to him in forgiveness. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

﴿But whoever repents﴾: i.e., returns from theft to Allah. ﴿After his wrongdoing﴾: i.e., his stealing. ﴿And makes amends﴾: i.e., his conduct. ﴿Indeed, Allah will turn to him﴾: i.e., He accepts his repentance, so He will not punish him in the Hereafter. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾: i.e., He is abundant in forgiveness, and for this reason He accepts his repentance. This is a justification (ta'lil) for what precedes it.

Abu al-Su'ud said: The mention of the Glorious Name here serves to indicate the reason for the ruling and to affirm the independence of the sentence.

And likewise in His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[40] ﴿Do you not know that to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth? He punishes whom He wills and forgives whom He wills, and Allah is over all things competent.﴾

﴿Do you not know that to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth?﴾ The title of divinity is the basis for the rulings of their sovereignty. The interrogative is for affirming knowledge, and its purpose is to cite this as evidence of His power, exalted is He, over the punishment and forgiveness that follow, in the most eloquent and complete manner. That is: Do you not know that He has the overpowering authority and the dazzling dominion, which necessitate complete power over the total disposal of them and of what is in them? ﴿He punishes whom He wills and forgives whom He wills.﴾ Punishment is mentioned first because the context is one of warning, so it is fitting to mention first what suits it of deterrents: ﴿And Allah is over all things competent﴾, and among that is punishment and forgiveness.

(p-١٩٨六) Caution (tanbih):

The majority of scholars hold that the repentance (tawbah) of a thief removes from him the hudud (the prescribed penalties) of Allah. As for the right of the human being (haqq al-adami), namely the amputation and the return of the property or its equivalent, it is not removed by his repentance.

Abu Hanifah said: Whenever the hand is amputated, and the property has been destroyed in his possession, he does not return its equivalent. The Sunnah has shown that if the owner pardons him before the matter is raised to the imam (ruler), the amputation falls away.

Ibn Majah narrated from Tha'labah al-Ansari: "That Umar ibn Samurah came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: O Messenger of Allah! I have stolen a camel belonging to the family of so-and-so, so purify me. The Prophet (ﷺ) sent to them, and they said: We have missed a camel of ours. He ordered it, and his hand was cut off." Tha'labah (one of the narrators in the chain) said: I looked at him when his hand fell, and he was saying: Praise be to Allah who has purified me from you. You wanted to bring my body into the Fire.

Imam Ahmad narrated from Abdullah ibn Amr: "That a woman stole during the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Those whom she had stolen from brought her and said: O Messenger of Allah! This woman has stolen from us. Her people said: We will ransom her (meaning her family). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: Cut off her hand. Her right hand was cut off. The woman said: Is there any repentance for me, O Messenger of Allah? He said: Yes, today you are free from your sin as on the day your mother bore you. So Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed in Surah al-Ma'idah: ﴿But whoever repents after his wrongdoing﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 39], to the end of the verse."

Ibn Kathir said: This woman is the Makhzumiyyah who stole, and her report is established in the two Sahihs (p-١٩٨٧) through the narration of al-Zuhri from Aishah: "That a woman stole during the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) during the conquest. Her people fled to Usamah ibn Zayd, asking him to intercede for them. Urwah said: When Usamah spoke to him about her, the face of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) changed color, and he said: Do you speak to me about one of the hudud of Allah? Usamah said: Ask forgiveness for me, O Messenger of Allah.

When evening came, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood to deliver a sermon, praised Allah with what is fitting for Him, and then said: As for what follows. Surely what destroyed the people before you was that when a noble person stole among them, they left him, and when a weak person stole among them, they enforced the hadd upon him. By Him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad! Even if Fatimah daughter of Muhammad had stolen, I would have cut off her hand.

Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ordered that woman, and her hand was cut off. Her repentance was good after that, and she married. Aishah said: She used to come after that, and I would raise her needs to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." This is the wording of Muslim. In another wording of his, from Aishah, she said: "There was a Makhzumi woman who would borrow goods and deny them, so the Prophet (ﷺ) ordered that her hand be cut off." And from Ibn Umar, he said: "A Makhzumi woman would borrow goods on the tongues of her neighbors and deny them, so the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ordered that her hand be cut off." Narrated by Imam Ahmad, Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i, and this is the wording of (p-١٩٨٨) the latter. In another of his wordings: "A woman used to borrow jewelry from people and then keep it, so the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: Stand up, O Bilal! Take her by the hand and cut it off."

The interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:

[41] ﴿O Messenger, let not those hasten to disbelief grieve you, those who say with their mouths, "We believe," but their hearts have not believed; and among those who are Jews, who are avid listeners to falsehood, avid listeners to another people who have not come to you. They distort words from their places. They say, "If you are given this, then take it; but if you are not given it, then beware." And whoever Allah wills to test, you will not avail him anything against Allah. Those are the ones for whom Allah did not will to purify their hearts. For them in this world is disgrace, and for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment.﴾

﴿O Messenger, let not you be grieved﴾ is a prohibition. Abu al-Baqa' (a grammarian and commentator) said: the preferred reading is opening the yā' and dhamming the zāy (yaḥzunka). It is also read with a ḍammah on the yā' and a kasrah on the zāy, from (aḥzanani), and this is a dialect (lughah).

﴿Those who hasten to disbelief﴾ means: in displaying it, by what appear from them as signs of plotting against Islam and of allegiance to the disbelievers.

﴿Among those who say, "We believe," with their mouths﴾ means: with their tongues. It is related to (qālū) (said).

﴿But their hearts have not believed﴾: these are the hypocrites. That is: do not concern yourself with them, for I am your helper against them.

﴿And among those who are Jews﴾ is coordinated with ﴿among those who said﴾. They are the Jews of the Banu Qurayzah, Ka'b and his companions.

﴿Avid listeners to falsehood﴾ is the predicate of an omitted subject, that is: they are avid listeners. The lām (li-) is either to strengthen the governing verb, or to imply in listening the meaning of acceptance, or it is the lām of purpose (kay), with the object omitted. The meaning is: they are excessive in listening to the lie that their rabbis have fabricated, or in accepting it. Or: they are avid listeners of your news in order to lie against you, by addition and subtraction, spreading rumours and terrifying.

In al-Iklil (a work of exegesis by al-Suyuti) it is stated that His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿avid listeners to falsehood﴾, indicates that the listener to what is forbidden is like its speaker in sin.

﴿Avid listeners to another people who have not come to you﴾ means: they did not attend your gathering and kept away from it, out of extreme hatred. That is: they accept from the rabbis and from those extremists in enmity who cannot bear to look at you. It was said: they are the Jews of Khaybar, and the avid listeners are the Banu Qurayzah.

﴿They distort the words﴾ means: the words of the Torah concerning the rulings.

﴿From after their places﴾ means: the places where Allah placed them.

Ibn Kathir said: that is, they handle it in other than its proper interpretation, and they alter it after they had understood it, while they know.

﴿They say, "If you are given this"﴾ means: if you are given this altered text, displaced from its places, from the Messenger, may the prayers and peace of Allah be upon him: ﴿then take it﴾, that is, act upon it, for it is the truth. ﴿But if you are not given it﴾, by which the Messenger gives you a ruling contrary to it: ﴿then beware﴾, that is, of accepting it, and beware of it! For it is falsehood and error.

Ibn Kathir said: It was said that it was revealed concerning a group of Jews who killed a slain man and said: "Come, let us take our dispute to Muhammad. If he rules with blood-money, accept it; but if he rules with retaliation (qisas), do not listen to him."

The sound view is that it was revealed concerning the two Jews who committed adultery. They had altered the Book of Allah that was in their hands regarding the command to stone whoever among them was married (muhsan). They distorted it and agreed among themselves on flogging one hundred lashes, tahmim (blackening the face), and mounting them backwards on a donkey. When that incident occurred after the Hijrah, they said among themselves: "Come, let us take our dispute to him. If he rules with flogging and tahmim, then take it from him and make it a proof between you and Allah, and he would be a prophet of Allah who has ruled with that."
