Moreover, exaggeration clings more to the Christians than to the Jews, as is not hidden. And God knows best.

Then God, exalted is He, informed that He cursed the disbelievers among the Children of Israel through what He sent down upon David and Jesus, peace be upon them both, because of their disobedience and the major sins that He enumerated. So He, glorified is He, said:

The commentary on His words, may He be exalted:

[78] ﴿Those who disbelieved among the Children of Israel were cursed upon the tongue of David and Jesus, son of Mary. That is because they disobeyed and used to transgress.﴾

﴿Those who disbelieved among the Children of Israel were cursed﴾, i.e., Allah, mighty and majestic, cursed them. ﴿Upon the tongue of David and Jesus, son of Mary﴾, i.e., upon the tongues of the two of them. The word "tongue" is given in the singular because there is no ambiguity, if by "tongue" is meant the organ. It has also been said that what is meant is speech and what was revealed to the two of them. Thus says al-'Inayah (al-Babarti, a super-commentary on al-Kashshaf).

﴿That﴾, i.e., their dreadful curse, ﴿is because they disobeyed and used to transgress﴾, by killing the prophets and making lawful what is forbidden.

**The discussion of the words of God, the Exalted: [79]** ﴿They did not forbid one another from any wrong they committed. Wretched indeed was what they used to do.﴾

﴿They did not forbid one another from any wrong they committed﴾ means: they did not forbid one another from committing sins and prohibited acts. Then He censured them for this, to warn against committing the like of what they committed, and so He said: ﴿Wretched indeed was what they used to do﴾, emphasized with the oath-particle lam (of asseveration), as an expression of wonder at the evil of their conduct, especially since it led them to the great curse that has been explained.

Observations:

First: The verse indicates the permissibility of cursing them.

Second: The verse also indicates the prohibition of means (dharai', "pretexts") that nullify the objectives of the Sharia. This is because most exegetes have related that those whom Dawud (peace be upon him) cursed were the people of Ayla who transgressed on the Sabbath and hunted fish in it. Their story will come in (al-A'raf).

Third: It also indicates the obligation of forbidding wrong (al-nahy 'an al-munkar).

Al-Hakim said: It also indicates that abandoning the forbidding of wrong is among the major sins.

Fourth: Imam Ahmad related regarding the meaning of the verse, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "When the Children of Israel fell into sins, their scholars forbade them, but they did not desist. So they sat with them in their gatherings and in their markets, ate with them and drank with them. So God struck the hearts of some of them against others, and cursed them upon the tongue of Dawud and Isa son of Maryam, that for what they disobeyed and used to transgress." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) was reclining, then he sat up and said: "No, by Him in whose hand is my soul! Until you restrain them upon the truth, restraining them firmly." Its meaning: you turn them toward it. Al-Tirmidhi related it and said: Hasan gharib.

Abu Dawud also narrated it from him, saying: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "The first deficiency that entered upon the Children of Israel was that a man would meet a man and say: 'O this one, fear God, and leave what you are doing, for it is not lawful for you.' Then he would meet him the next day, and that would not prevent him from being his eating companion, his drinking companion, and his sitting companion. When they did that, God struck the hearts of some of them against others, then said: ﴿Those who disbelieved among the Children of Israel were cursed﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 78] — to His saying — ﴿are defiantly disobedient﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 78-79]. Then He said: 'Nay, by God! You must enjoin what is right, you must forbid what is wrong, you must seize the hand of the wrongdoer, and you must restrain him upon the truth, restraining him firmly, or you will surely confine him to the truth by confinement.'"

In one narration he added: "Or God will surely strike the hearts of some of you against others, then curse you as He cursed them."

Likewise al-Tirmidhi related it and graded it hasan. And Ibn Majah.

The hadiths on enjoining good and forbidding wrong are numerous, and among those suitable to this context are:

What Imam Ahmad and al-Tirmidhi related from Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman: that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul! You must enjoin what is right and you must forbid what is wrong, or God will surely soon send upon you a punishment from Him, then you will call upon Him and He will not respond to you."

And in the Two Sahihs, from Abu Sa'id, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Whoever among you sees a wrong, let him change it with his hand. If he is unable, then with his tongue. If he is unable, then with his heart. And that is the weakest of faith."

Imam Ahmad related from Adi ibn Umayra (may God be pleased with him), who said: I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: "God does not punish the common people for the deed of the elite until they see wrong among them while they are able to change it but do not change it. When they do that, God punishes the elite and the common people alike."

Ibn Majah related from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: "God will indeed question the servant on the Day of Resurrection until He says: 'What prevented you, when you saw wrong, from changing it?' When God inspires a servant with his argument, he will say: 'O Lord! I hoped in You, and I feared people.'"

The Hafiz Ibn Kathir said: Ibn Majah alone narrated it, and its chain is acceptable.

Imam Ahmad and al-Tirmidhi related from Hudhayfah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "It is not befitting for a Muslim to humiliate himself." It was said: "How does he humiliate himself?" He said: "He exposes himself to a trial he cannot bear."

Al-Tirmidhi said: Hasan gharib.

Ibn Majah related from Anas ibn Malik, who said: "It was said: 'O Messenger of God! When do we abandon enjoining good and forbidding wrong?' He said: 'When there appears among you what appeared among the nations before you.' We said: 'O Messenger of God! What appeared among the nations before us?' He said: 'Kingship among your young, immorality among your elders, and knowledge among your lowest.'"

Zayd ibn Yahya al-Khuza'i, one of its narrators, said: The meaning of the Prophet's (ﷺ) words "and knowledge among your lowest" is when knowledge is held by the wicked.

Ibn Majah alone narrated it. It has a supporting narration in the hadith of Abu Tha'labah, which will come, God willing, at His saying: ﴿Those who have gone astray will not harm you﴾. Ibn Kathir stated this.

I say: These hadiths are only relied upon by the weak, such as the scholars and leaders. As for those who hold binding authority and complete standing, it is far-fetched that these terrifying promises would benefit them, and these dreadful warnings hover over their heads. Therefore the Allamah al-Zamakhshari said: "Alas, the grief over Muslims in their turning away from the door of mutual forbidding of wrongs, and their little concern for it, as if it were not from the religion of Islam at all, despite what they recite of the Book of God and the exaggerated emphasis it contains on this matter." What supports what is here has already passed at His saying: ﴿Why do the rabbis and scholars not forbid them?﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 63], so reflect.

Fifth: Al-Zamakhshari said: If you ask: how did the abandonment of forbidding wrong come to be explained as disobedience and transgression? I say: Because God, the Exalted, commanded forbidding, so neglecting it was disobedience, and that is transgression.

When the Exalted described their predecessors with what has passed, He described those present with His saying:

(p-2115) The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[80] ﴿You see many of them turning in friendship to those who disbelieve. Wretched is what their souls have sent ahead for them, that Allah has become wrathful against them, and in the punishment they will abide eternally.﴾

﴿You see many of them﴾ i.e., of the People of the Book: ﴿turning in friendship to those who disbelieve﴾ i.e., they take as allies the polytheists (mushrikun), out of hatred for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

Al-Razi said: What is meant by them is Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf and his companions, when they incited the polytheists against the Messenger (ﷺ). We have mentioned this in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they say to those who disbelieve, "These are better guided in the way than those who believe"﴾ [An-Nisa: 51].

﴿Wretched is what their souls have sent ahead for them﴾ i.e., wretched is the thing they sent forward for their return (to Allah). His saying, exalted is He: ﴿that Allah has become wrathful against them﴾ is the object of the dispraise (al-makhsus bil-dhamm), by omitting the modified noun (al-mudaf) and placing the modified-to noun (al-mudaf ilayhi) in its stead, to draw attention to the complete connection and linkage between the two, as if they were one thing, and as an exaggeration in dispraise. The meaning is: ﴿Wretched﴾ is what they provisioned for themselves in the Hereafter, which necessitated the wrath of Allah, exalted is He, against them. ﴿And in the punishment﴾ i.e., the punishment of Hell, ﴿they will abide eternally.﴾

The discussion of the words of God Most High:

[81] ﴿Had they believed in God, and in the Prophet, and in what was sent down to him, they would not have taken them as allies; but many of them are defiantly disobedient.﴾

﴿Had they been﴾, i.e. those who take as allies the worshippers of idols from among the People of the Book, ﴿believing in God and the Prophet﴾, i.e. their prophet Musa (peace be upon him), ﴿and in what was sent down to him﴾, i.e. the Torah, ﴿they would not have taken them as allies﴾, since faith in God prevents one from allying with one who worships other than Him; ﴿but many of them are defiantly disobedient﴾, i.e. they have departed from their religion, or they persist in their hypocrisy. The meaning is that their alliance (p-2116) with the polytheists is by itself sufficient proof of their hypocrisy, and that their faith is not true faith, because the prohibition of such alliance is emphatically stated in the Torah and in the law of Musa (peace be upon him). When they did this, it became clear that their aim was not to uphold the religion of Musa (peace be upon him), but rather leadership and status (riyasah wa jah), so they strive to attain it by whatever means they can. For this reason God Most High described them with defiance (fisq).

There is another interpretation of the verse: that the meaning is, "Had they — i.e. the hypocrites among the People of the Book who claim to believe — believed in Muhammad (ﷺ) and the Qur'an with true faith, they would not have committed what they committed, of allying with the disbelievers in secret."

The first interpretation is more upright, and God knows best.

Then God Most High emphasized what preceded of the faults of the Jews with His words:

**The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted Is He:**

﴿You will surely find the most intense of people in enmity toward the believers to be the Jews and those who associated others with God; and you will surely find the nearest of them in affection toward the believers to be those who say, "We are Christians." That is because among them are priests and monks, and because they are not arrogant.﴾

﴿You will surely find the most intense of people in enmity toward the believers to be the Jews and those who associated others with God.﴾ The Jews opposed them because they believed in Jesus and Muhammad (ﷺ), and the polytheists opposed them for their monotheism and their affirmation of the prophethood of the prophets. This was indicated by al-Mahayimi.

Others said: [the enmity was due to] the intensity of their refusal, the multiplication of their disbelief, their immersion in following their desires, their reliance on blind imitation (taqlid), their distance from verification (tahqiq), their habituation to rebellion and defiance against the prophets, their audacity in denying them, and their hostility toward them. For this reason, they killed many of them, and even intended to kill the Messenger of God (ﷺ) more than once, poisoned him, bewitched him, and incited their counterparts among the polytheists against him.

In placing (the Jews) before (the polytheists), after both were linked in one clause, there is an indication of their precedence over them in enmity, just as their being placed first in His words, ﴿And you will surely find them the most avid of people for life, and of those who associated others with God﴾ [al-Baqarah: 96], signals their precedence in greed.

﴿And you will surely find the nearest of them in affection toward the believers to be those who say, "We are Christians."﴾ This is due to the gentleness of their side and the scarcity of rancor in their hearts.

Ibn Kathir said: This is only because of what is in their hearts, since they were upon the religion of the Messiah, with its tenderness and compassion, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And We placed in the hearts of those who followed him compassion and mercy and monasticism﴾ [al-Hadid: 27]. And in their book: "Whoever strikes you on your right cheek, turn to him your left cheek." Fighting is not prescribed in their religion. End of quotation.

Also, among the doctrines of the Jews is that it is obligatory to inflict harm upon whoever opposes their religion by any means whatsoever, such as killing, plundering wealth, and the like, whereas this is forbidden in the view of the Christians. Thus the difference is established.

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Abu Hurayrah, as a marfu' report: "No Jew is alone with a Muslim but he intends to kill him."

Due to the Christians' great concern with knowledge and asceticism, which calls for little hatred and envy and gentleness of disposition, as is indicated by His words, exalted is He: ﴿That﴾, i.e., their being nearer in affection to the believers, ﴿is because among them﴾, i.e., due to the fact that among them, ﴿are qissisin﴾, i.e., scholars, ﴿and monks﴾, i.e., worshippers who devote themselves [to worship], ﴿and because they are not arrogant﴾, i.e., they are humble in their meekness and do not act arrogantly as the Jews do. In the verse there is evidence that devotion to knowledge, turning away from base desires, and freedom from arrogance are praiseworthy, even if they come from a disbeliever.

(p-2118)

**A Subtle Point:**

Al-Nasir said in *al-Intisaf*:

He, exalted is He, said "those who say, 'We are Christians'" and did not say "the Christians," as an allusion to the stubbornness of the Jews in disbelief and their refusal to comply with the command. For the Jews were told: ﴿Enter the Holy Land which God has prescribed for you, and do not turn back on your heels﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 21], and they responded by saying: ﴿So go, you and your Lord, and fight; indeed we are sitting here﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 24]. The Christians said: "We are the helpers of God," and for this reason they were called Nasara (Christians). Likewise, it occurred at the beginning of this surah: ﴿And from those who said, "We are Christians," We took their covenant, but they forgot a portion of what they had been reminded of﴾. So that was attributed to their saying, and the reference by "this" is to their saying "We are the helpers of God." (p-2119) Here, however, He mentioned it as a notice that they did not remain firm on the covenant nor on what they had said about being the helpers of God. In the second verse, He mentioned it as a notice that their condition is nearer than that of the Jews, because when the command came to them, they did not confront it with rejection as the Jews did; rather, they said: "We are the helpers of God," whereas the Jews said: ﴿So go, you and your Lord...﴾ This is its secret. And God knows best.

The discussion on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[83] ﴿When they hear what has been sent down to the Messenger, you see their eyes overflowing with tears because of the truth they recognize. They say: "Our Lord, we have believed, so record us among the witnesses."﴾

﴿When they hear what has been sent down to the Messenger﴾ is coordinated (ʿaṭf) with ﴿they are not arrogant﴾ (لا يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ). Abu al-Baqa' said: It is permissible for it to be a new sentence (mustaʾnaf) in wording, even though it is related in meaning to what precedes it. That is: when they hear the Qur'an. ﴿You see their eyes overflowing﴾ means they pour out, ﴿with tears﴾ resulting from the combination of the heat of love and fear together with the coolness of certainty. ﴿Because of the truth they recognize﴾ means: from their own Scripture, which they found to be more complete and superior to it; or from what was sent down upon the Messenger (ﷺ), which is the truth; or from the description of Muhammad (ﷺ) and his attributes in their Scripture. ﴿They say﴾ means: out of their not being arrogant, ﴿Our Lord, we have believed﴾ means: in You, in what You have sent down, and in Your Messenger Muhammad, ﴿so record us among the witnesses﴾ means: those who bear witness that it is the truth, or to his prophethood. Al-Hakim narrated it and authenticated it, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: That is, with the community of Muhammad (ﷺ), and his community are the witnesses. They bear witness for their Prophet that he has conveyed, and for the messengers that they have conveyed.

And His saying, exalted is He:

(p-2120) On the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[84] ﴿And why should we not believe in God and in what has come to us of the truth, while we long that our Lord would admit us along with the righteous people?﴾

﴿And why should we not believe in God﴾: This is a denunciation expressing that it is improbable that faith would be absent while its requirement is present, namely the hope (ṭamaʿ) of God's favour upon them by being granted the company of the righteous. ﴿And in what has come to us of the truth﴾, i.e., and in what has come to us of the Qur'an. Regarding its grammatical analysis (iʿrāb) there is another possibility that will come. ﴿And we long that our Lord would admit us along with the righteous people﴾: meaning, along with the community of Muhammad (ﷺ); or the meaning is: that our Lord would admit us into Paradise along with the prophets and the believers.

The interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:

﴿So Allah rewarded them for what they said: gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein; and that is the recompense of the doers of good.﴾

﴿So Allah rewarded them for what they said﴾ i.e., for what they spoke of, namely their saying: "Our Lord, we have believed," which proceeded from conviction, sincerity, and acknowledgment of the truth. ﴿gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾ i.e., beneath their trees and dwellings. ﴿rivers﴾ meaning rivers of water, milk, and honey. ﴿abiding therein﴾ i.e., remaining in the Garden, not dying and not being removed from it. ﴿and that is the recompense of the doers of good﴾ meaning the believers who affirm Divine oneness and are sincere in their faith.

Admonitions:

The first: The exegetes agreed that these four verses were revealed concerning the Negus (al-Najashi, the ruler of Abyssinia) and his companions, may Allah be pleased with them.

Ibn Abi Hatim related from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, Abu Bakr ibn Abd al-Rahman, and Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent Amr ibn Umayya al-Damri and wrote a letter with him to the Negus. He arrived before the Negus, who read the letter of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Then he summoned Ja'far ibn Abi Talib and the Muhajirun with him, and sent for the monks and the priests. Then he ordered Ja'far ibn Abi Talib, who recited to them Surah Maryam. They believed in the Qur'an and their eyes overflowed with tears. They are the ones concerning whom Allah revealed: ﴿And you will surely find the nearest of them in affection to the believers﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 82] - up to His saying: ﴿So register us among the witnesses﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 83]."

Ibn Abi Hatim also related from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: "The Negus sent thirty men from his best companions to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He recited to them Surah Ya-Sin, and they wept, so the verse was revealed concerning them."

al-Nasa'i related from Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr, who said: This verse was revealed concerning the Negus and his companions: ﴿And when they hear what has been revealed to the Messenger﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 83].

al-Tabarani related from Ibn Abbas and similar to it, more extensively.

- Thus it is in "Asbab al-Nuzul" of al-Suyuti -

Ibn Kathir said: Ali ibn Abi Talhah related from Ibn Abbas: This verse was revealed concerning the Negus and his companions, who, when Ja'far ibn Abi Talib recited the Qur'an to them in Abyssinia, wept until they dyed their beards with tears.

Ibn Kathir said: This statement is open to question, because this verse is Medinan, while the story of Ja'far with the Negus occurred before the Hijrah. End of quotation.

I say: His objection is answered, for he related in this verse, after the Hijrah, what occurred before it, and similar instances in the Revelation are numerous, with no difficulty in them. It is evident that the intended purpose of this verse is a rebuke of the obstinacy of the Jews who were around Medina, namely the Jews of Banu Qurayzah and al-Nadir, and also of the obstinacy of the polytheists, and the hardness of the hearts of both groups, and that it was more fitting for them to acknowledge the truth as the Negus and his companions acknowledged it. Ibn Kathir also said: This category of Christians is the one mentioned in His saying, Exalted is He: (p-2122) ﴿And among the People of the Book are those who believe in Allah and in what has been revealed to you and what has been revealed to them, humbling themselves before Allah﴾ [Al 'Imran: 199] and so on. They are those concerning whom Allah said: ﴿Those to whom We gave the Book before it, they believe in it﴾ [al-Qasas: 52] ﴿And when it is recited to them, they say: "We believed in it; indeed it is the truth from our Lord. Indeed we were Muslims before it"﴾ [al-Qasas: 53] up to His saying: ﴿We do not seek the ignorant﴾ [al-Qasas: 55]. End of quotation.

The cause of the companions' emigration to the land of Abyssinia was that the Quraysh conspired to seduce the believers from their religion. Every tribe leapt upon those among them who had embraced Islam, harmed them, and tortured them. Some of them were seduced, and Allah protected whom He willed of them.

Ibn Ishaq, may Allah have mercy on him, said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw what afflictions his companions suffered, while he himself was in safety by his station with Allah and by his uncle Abu Talib, and that he could not protect them from the affliction they were in, he said to them: "If you went out to the land of Abyssinia, for there is a king there under whom no one is wronged, and it is a land of truthfulness, until Allah grants you relief from what you are in." 

So at that time the Muslims among the companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out to the land of Abyssinia, fearing the trial, and they fled to Allah with their religion. This was the first emigration in Islam.

(p-2123) All who joined the land of Abyssinia and emigrated there among the Muslims, apart from their sons who went out with them as children and were born there, numbered eighty-three men, if Ammar ibn Yasir was among them, and he was uncertain about it.

Then Ibn Ishaq related with his chain to Umm Salamah, wife of the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: When we alighted in the land of Abyssinia, we were neighbored there by the best of neighbors, the Negus. We were safe in our religion, we worshipped Allah, Exalted is He, we were not harmed, and we heard nothing we disliked. When this reached the Quraysh, they conspired among themselves to send to the Negus two strong men from among them, and to give the Negus gifts of the finest goods of Mecca. Among the things most pleasing to him from them was leather. So they gathered a great amount of leather for him. They left none of his patriarchs (batariqah) without giving him a gift. Then they sent with that Abd Allah ibn Abi Rabi'ah and Amr ibn al-As, and instructed them with their command, saying to them: "Hand to each patriarch his gift before you speak to the Negus about them. Then present to the Negus his gifts. Then ask him to hand them over to you before he speaks with them." She said: So the two set out until they arrived before the Negus, while we were with him in the best dwelling, with the best neighbor. No patriarch remained among his patriarchs without them handing him his gift before they spoke to the Negus, and they said to each patriarch of them: "A band of foolish youths has taken refuge in the land of our king from us; they have left the religion of their people and did not enter your religion, and they have brought a novel religion that neither we nor you know. We have sent to the king the nobles of their people to return them to them. So when we speak to the king about them, advise him to hand them over to us and not to speak with them, for their people are better informed about them (i.e., more perceptive about them) and more knowing of what they reproached them for." They said to them: "Yes." 

(p-2124) Then the two presented their gifts to the Negus, and he accepted them from them, and then they spoke to him what they had said to each patriarch. 

She said: Nothing was more hateful to Abd Allah ibn Abi Rabi'ah and Amr ibn al-As than that the Negus should hear their speech. She said: So his patriarchs around him said: "They have spoken truly, O king! Their people are better informed about them and more knowing of what they reproached them for. So hand them over to them, and let them return them to their lands and their people." She said: The Negus became angry and said: "No, by Allah! I will not hand them over to them. A people who have neighbored me, dwelt in my land, and chosen me over others will not be given up until I call them and ask them about what these two say about them. If they are as these two say, I will hand them over to them and return them to their people. If they are otherwise, I will protect them from them and give them the best neighborliness for as long as they are my neighbors."

She said: Then he sent for the companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and summoned them, and when his messenger came to them they gathered. Then some of them said to others: "What will you say to the man when you come to him?" They said: "By Allah! We will say what we know, and what our Prophet commanded us, whatever the outcome may be." When they came, the Negus had summoned his bishops, who spread their scriptures around him. He asked them and said: "What is this religion from which you have separated from your people, and did not enter into my religion or the religion of any of these creeds?" She said: The one who spoke to him was Ja'far ibn Abi Talib, who said to him: "O king! We were a people of the Jahiliyyah. We worshipped idols, ate carrion, committed indecencies, severed the ties of kinship, and broke the duties of neighborliness. The strong among us devoured the weak. We remained so until Allah sent to us a messenger from among us, whose lineage, truthfulness, trustworthiness, and chastity we knew. He called to Allah that we should affirm His oneness and worship Him, and renounce what we and our fathers worshipped besides Him of stones and idols. He commanded us to speak truth, to fulfill trusts, to maintain ties of kinship, to be good neighbors, to refrain from what is forbidden and from bloodshed, and he forbade us from indecencies, false speech, consuming the wealth of orphans, and slandering chaste women. He commanded us to worship Allah alone without associating anything with Him, and commanded us to prayer, zakat, and fasting." She said: He enumerated to him the matters of Islam. "So we believed him, affirmed him, and followed him in what he brought from Allah. We worshipped Allah alone and did not associate anything with Him, (p-2125) and we forbade what He forbade us and made lawful what He made lawful for us. Then our people transgressed against us, tortured us, and tried to turn us from our religion to return us to the worship of idols instead of the worship of Allah, Exalted is He, and to make lawful for us the filthy things we used to consider lawful. When they overpowered us, oppressed us, constricted us, and came between us and our religion, we went out to your land, chose you over others, desired your protection, and hoped that we would not be wronged in your presence, O king!" 

He said: The Negus said to him: "Do you have with you anything of what was brought from Allah?" She said: Ja'far said to him: "Yes!" The Negus said to him: "Then recite it to me." She said: He recited to him the beginning of Kaf Ha Ya 'Ain Sad. She said: By Allah, the Negus wept until his beard was drenched, and his bishops wept until they drenched their scriptures when they heard what he recited to them. Then the Negus said: "Indeed this, and that which Jesus brought, comes out of one niche. Go, by Allah! I will not hand them over to you, and they will not be harmed."

She said: When the two left his presence, Amr ibn al-As said: "By Allah! I will go to him tomorrow concerning them with something by which I will uproot their green (i.e., their tree from which they branched out)."

She said: Abd Allah ibn Abi Rabi'ah, who was the more pious of the two men among us, said to him: "Do not do that, for they have kinship ties, even though they have opposed us." He said: "By Allah! I will tell him that they claim Jesus son of Mary is a servant."

She said: Then the next day he went to him and said: "O king! They say a grave thing about Jesus son of Mary. Send for them and ask them what they say about him." She said: So he sent for them to ask them about him.

She said: Nothing like it had ever befallen us. The people gathered, and some of them said to others: "What will you say about Jesus son of Mary if he asks you about him?" They said: "By Allah! We will say what Allah said and what our Prophet brought us, whatever the outcome may be." He said: So when they entered upon him, he said to them: "What do you say about Jesus son of Mary?" She said: Ja'far ibn Abi Talib said: "We say about him what our Prophet (ﷺ) brought us: He is the servant of Allah, His messenger, His spirit, and His word which He cast to Mary the virgin, the pure." She said: The Negus struck the ground with his hand and took a stick from it, then said: "By Allah, Jesus son of Mary does not exceed what you have said by this stick." She said: His patriarchs snorted around him when he said what he said. He said: "Even if you snort, by Allah! Go, for you are secure (shiyum) in my land, and whoever insults you will pay a penalty." He said it three times.

Then he said: "I would not love to have a mountain of gold (dabr, the mountain) and that I had harmed a man among you. Return to them their gifts, for I have no need of them."

She said: The two left his presence humiliated, their gifts returned to them, and what they had come with rejected, and we remained with him in the best abode with the best neighbor.

Then Ibn Ishaq related in his account: The Negus took a document and wrote in it: "He testifies that there is no god but Allah, and that Muhammad is His servant and messenger. And he testifies that Jesus son of Mary is His servant, His messenger, His spirit, and His word which He cast to Mary." End of quotation.

The Islam of the Negus is well known, and when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) died, he prayed over him despite the distance between the lands.

Shams al-Din ibn al-Qayyim mentioned in "Zad al-Ma'ad" that their emigration to Abyssinia was in the fifth year of the Prophethood.

The second admonition:

In the verse there is evidence that what is prescribed when reciting the Qur'an is humble submission (khushu') and weeping. There is a report: "Weep, and if you do not find weeping, then force yourselves to weep." Al-Mundhiri (al-Mundhiri) cited it in *al-Targhib wal-Tarhib* on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr. He said: al-Hakim narrated it as a marfu' (traced to the Prophet ﷺ) report and graded it sound. What is meant is that the heart be saturated with it, and that fear be reverence before God, exalted is He.

The third point concerns His saying: ﴿They say, "Our Lord, we have believed"﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 83], and His saying: ﴿So God rewarded them for what they said﴾. This is evidence that affirmation by the tongue (iqrar) is included in faith (iman), as is the position of the jurists (fuqaha'). The Karramiyya (a sect) relied on His saying "for what they said" to argue that faith is merely speech. However, the praise for the overflowing of tears in the preceding context, and for good conduct in the present context, refutes that. How could mere speech be faith when God says: ﴿And among the people are those who say, "We believe in God and the Last Day," but they are not believers﴾ [al-Baqarah: 8]? He denied them faith despite their saying "We believe in God," because there was no assent in the heart.

The people of gnosis (ma'rifah) said: What is found in them consists of three things: weeping over neglect, supplication over giving, and contentment with the decree. Whoever claims gnosis and does not have these three is not truthful in his claim! Reported by al-Nasafi.

Al-Khazin said: He attached the reward only to the mere speech because their described state had already preceded, showing their sincerity in what they said. That is the gnosis and the weeping, which indicate the reality of sincerity and the humbling of the heart. For when speech is accompanied by gnosis, it is the true faith promised with reward.

Al-Razi said: When gnosis, sincerity and complete submission were achieved, and then speech was added to it, faith was thereby perfected.

The fourth point: His saying ﴿and what has come to us﴾ may be in a position of genitive (jarr) (i.e., grammatically governed by a preposition), meaning "and by what has come to us." ﴿of the truth﴾ is a circumstantial (hal) phrase (an adverbial accusative describing the state) of the concealed subject pronoun, or an inessential complement (laghw, i.e., an adverbial phrase not essential to the sentence structure) connected to "came," meaning "and by what has come to us from God." It may also be a subject (mubtada'), with "of the truth" as the predicate (khabar), and the clause is then in the position of a circumstantial phrase. His saying ﴿and we aspire﴾ may be coordinated with "we believe," meaning "and why should we not aspire." It may also be that the implied sense is "and we aspire," so the clause is a circumstantial phrase from the pronoun of the subject in "we believe." Reported by Abu al-Baqa'.

The discussion of His saying, may He be exalted:

[86] ﴿And those who disbelieved and denied Our signs — those are the companions of the Blazing Fire.﴾

﴿And those who disbelieved and denied Our signs — those are the companions of the Blazing Fire.﴾ That is: those who rejected the truth that came to them and denied the proofs and evidences of Allah — those are the companions of the Blazing Fire, i.e., the fire of intense heat, a fitting recompense.

[p. 2128]

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[87] ﴿O you who have believed, do not forbid the good things that Allah has made lawful for you, and do not transgress. Indeed, Allah does not love the transgressors.﴾

﴿O you who have believed, do not forbid the good things that Allah has made lawful for you﴾ means: that which is good and pleasant of it. It is as if, when the preceding verses included praise of the Christians for their asceticism (al-tarhib), and their urging to break the self and renounce desires, He followed that with a prohibition against excess in this, by forbidding the pleasures of what is permitted by the Sharia. Then He indicated that this is transgression, by His saying, glorified is He: ﴿and do not transgress﴾, meaning: beyond what Allah, glorified and exalted is He, has set as limits, by making the lawful unlawful. Or: do not transgress in the consumption of what is lawful, by exceeding its limit into extravagance, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Eat and drink, but do not be extravagant﴾ [al-A'raf: 31], and He said: ﴿And those who, when they spend, are neither extravagant nor stingy, but are ever justly balanced between that﴾ [al-Furqan: 67]. Or: do not transgress against yourselves and your families by withholding their rights. Or: do not transgress the bounds of what Allah has made lawful for you towards what He has made unlawful for you. ﴿Indeed, Allah does not love the transgressors﴾ in all that has been mentioned. This is a justification for what precedes it.

**On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:**

[88] ﴿And eat of what Allah has provided for you as lawful and good, and fear Allah, in whom you are believers.﴾

﴿And eat of what Allah has provided for you as lawful and good﴾: that is, eat what is lawful and good for you of what Allah has provided. Accordingly, ḥalālan ("lawful") is the object of ﴿kulū﴾ ("eat"), and mimmā ("of what") is a circumstantial phrase (ḥāl) related to it, or it is connected to ﴿kulū﴾. Or, mimmā is the object, and ḥalālan is a circumstantial phrase (ḥāl) from mā ("what") or from its omitted pronoun referring back to it. Or, ḥalālan is an adjective of an omitted verbal noun, meaning: (p-2129) eating that is lawful. His words, exalted is He, ﴿and fear Allah﴾, are an emphasis of the injunction to what He has commanded, and He strengthened this with His words ﴿in whom you are believers﴾, because belief in Him obliges taqwā (God-consciousness, fear of God) in adhering to what He has commanded and in refraining from what He has forbidden.

Al-Mahāyimī said: What your faith requires is that you not alter anything of the rulings of your religion, that you not oppose its rulings even with aversion from your own selves, and that you fear Him by not establishing principles that contradict the principles of the Sharia. Rather, the most that is permitted is to derive meanings from the knowledge of the Sharia that confirm its requirement.

**Remarks:**

**First:** Concerning what has been narrated about the occasion of its revelation:

Al-Tirmidhī narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both: "A man came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: 'When I eat meat, I am aroused toward women and my desire takes hold of me, so I have made meat forbidden to myself.' Then Allah, exalted is He, revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, do not forbid﴾ [al-Mā'ida: 87], the verse."

Ibn Abī Ḥātim narrated from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa, from Ibn ʿAbbās: "This verse was revealed concerning a group of the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ). They said: 'We will castrate ourselves, abandon the desires of this world, and wander in the earth as the monks do.' This reached the Prophet (ﷺ), so he sent for them and mentioned this to them. They said: 'Yes.' The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'But I fast and break my fast, I pray and sleep, and I marry women. Whoever takes my Sunna is of me, and whoever does not take my Sunna is not of me.'" Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar.

In the two Ṣaḥīḥs (Bukhārī and Muslim), from the ḥadīth of ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her: "Some people among the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) asked the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) about his practice in private. Some of them said: 'I will not eat meat.' Some said: 'I will not marry women.' Some said: 'I will not sleep on a bed.' This reached the Prophet (ﷺ), and he said: 'What is the matter with people who say such and such? But I fast and break my fast, I sleep and I stand in prayer, I eat meat, and I marry women. Whoever turns away from my Sunna is not of me.'" (p-2130)

Ibn Abī Ḥātim narrated that Ibn Masʿūd was approached by Maʿqil ibn Muqarrin, who said: "I have made my bed forbidden to myself." So he recited this verse to him.

He also narrated from Masrūq, who said: "We were with ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd. A udder (of meat) was brought, and a man withdrew. ʿAbdullāh said: 'Come near.' He said: 'I have made it forbidden to myself to eat it.' ʿAbdullāh said: 'Come near and eat, and make expiation for your oath.' And he recited this verse." Al-Ḥākim also narrated it.

**Second:** Some of the Zaydiyya said: The fruit of the verse is the prohibition against forbidding the good things of what is lawful. Al-Ḥākim mentioned that this prohibition may have several meanings, and there is no obstacle to understanding it as covering all of them: One of them: do not believe in its prohibition. Another: do not forbid it to others through legal opinion (fatwā) and judgment. Another: do not treat it as the forbidden things in the severity of avoidance. Another: do not bind yourselves to its prohibition by a vow or otherwise.

Al-Qāḍī said: Do not forbid the lawful through an action that proceeds from you, such as usurious transactions, mixing the lawful with what is usurped, and the pure with the impure.

Then he said: Two matters are connected to this. The first: If one forbids the lawful, is it obligatory for him to break the oath and retract? We say: The apparent meaning of the verse indicates this, and repentance is also required along with it.

The second matter: Is expiation (kaffāra) obligatory for him in that case? We say: This verse may be cited as evidence for the obligation, since a prohibition requires the corruption of what is prohibited. This question is one on which the scholars differ. End of quotation.

Ibn Kathīr said: al-Shāfiʿī held that whoever forbids food, clothing, or anything else, other than women, it is not forbidden to him, and there is no expiation for him either, because of the general wording of this verse. Also, the one who made meat forbidden to himself, as in the ḥadīth mentioned earlier, was not commanded by the Prophet (ﷺ) to make expiation.

Others, among them the Imam Aḥmad, held that whoever forbids something of those mentioned, expiation of an oath (kaffārat yamīn) becomes obligatory for him, just as when he binds himself to abandon it by an oath. Likewise, he is held accountable by the mere act of forbidding it to himself, as a binding obligation to what he committed himself to. This is the ruling Ibn ʿAbbās issued. And it is as in His words, exalted is He: ﴿O Prophet, why do you forbid what Allah has made lawful for you, seeking the approval of your wives? And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [al-Taḥrīm: 1], then He said: ﴿Allah has already ordained for you the dissolution of your oaths﴾ [al-Taḥrīm: 2], the verse. And so it is here: when He mentioned this ruling, He followed it with the verse that explains the expiation of the oath, which indicates that this is treated as an oath in requiring expiation. And Allah knows best.

(p-2132) In Zād al-Maʿād by Ibn al-Qayyim there is an important section on the ruling concerning one who forbids his slave-girl, his wife, or his property; it is worth consulting.

**Third:** This verse is a basis for abandoning excessive strictness (tanaṭṭuʿ) and harshness (tashaddud) in worship. Thus it is in al-Iklīl.

Ibn Jarīr said: It is not permitted for any of the Muslims to forbid anything that Allah has made lawful for His believing servants, upon himself, from the good foods, clothing, and marriages. For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) rejected celibacy (tabattul) proposed by ʿUthmān ibn Maẓʿūn. Thus it is established that there is no merit in abandoning anything that Allah has made lawful for His servants. The merit and righteousness lie only in doing what Allah has recommended to His servants, what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) practiced and established as a Sunna for his community, and what the rightly-guided Imams followed of his path, since the best guidance is the guidance of our Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ). If this is so, the error of one who prefers wearing hair and wool over cotton and linen, when he is able to wear these lawfully, becomes clear. And the error of one who prefers eating coarse food and abandoning meat and other things, out of fear of the incidental need for women.

He said: If someone supposes that the merit lies in something other than what we have said, namely, in wearing coarse clothing and eating coarse food as a hardship upon the self, and giving away the surplus value of these to people in need, then he has erred. That is because what is best for a person is the soundness of his self and assisting it in obeying its Lord. Nothing harms the body more than bad food, for it corrupts his intellect and weakens his faculties which Allah has made a means to obedience to Him. End of quotation.

Al-Rāzī has an excellent discussion here on the wisdom of this prohibition, supporting what has been mentioned. It should be consulted, for it is precious.

Al-Tirmidhī narrated from ʿĀʾisha: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) loved sweets and honey." He also narrated from Abū Hurayra: "A meat dish was brought to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the foreleg, which he liked, was lifted up to him, (p-2133) and he tore some of it with his teeth. ʿĀʾisha said: The foreleg was not the most beloved to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), but he did not find meat except occasionally, and the foreleg was hastened to him because it cooks the fastest." Al-Tirmidhī narrated it.

Al-Zamakhsharī related from al-Ḥasan that he was invited to a meal, along with Farqad al-Sabakhī and his companions. They sat at the table, on which were various dishes of fattened chicken, fālūdhaj (a sweet), and other things. Farqad withdrew to a corner, so al-Ḥasan asked: "Is he fasting?" They said: "No, but he dislikes these dishes." Al-Ḥasan turned to him and said: "O Furayqad! Do you see the saliva of the bee, with the finest wheat, with pure ghee, as something a Muslim should find fault with?"

Also from him: It was said to him: "So-and-so does not eat fālūdhaj and says: 'I cannot give thanks for it.'" He said: "Does he drink cold water?" They said: "Yes." He said: "He is ignorant. Allah's blessing upon him in cold water is greater than His blessing in fālūdhaj."

Also from him: Allah, exalted is He, taught His servants good manners and made their manners excellent. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Let the one of wealth spend from his wealth﴾ [al-Ṭalāq: 7]. Allah never faulted a people to whom He widened the world and who lived in comfort and obeyed Him, nor did He excuse a people from whom He withheld it and who disobeyed Him.

**Fourth:** Al-Rāzī said: He, exalted is He, did not say "eat what He has provided you" but said ﴿of what Allah has provided you﴾, and the word "min" (of) indicates partiality. It is as if He said: Limit your eating to a part, and direct the remainder to charities and good works, because this is guidance to abandoning extravagance (isrāf), as He said: ﴿and do not be extravagant﴾.

(p. 2134) The interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:

[89] ﴿Allah will not hold you accountable for the slips in your oaths, but He will hold you accountable for what you have bound by oaths. Its expiation is feeding ten needy people, from the average of what you feed your families, or clothing them, or freeing a slave. But whoever cannot find [the means], then fasting for three days. That is the expiation of your oaths when you have sworn. And guard your oaths. Thus Allah makes clear to you His verses, that you may be grateful.﴾

﴿Allah will not hold you accountable for the slips in your oaths﴾: The discussion of the unintended oath (al-laghw fi al-yamin) has already been given in (Surat al-Baqarah). It is what the tongue utters without intending to swear, such as a person saying: "No, by Allah!" and "Yes, by Allah!" The meaning of "holding accountable" here is holding accountable for sin and expiation. That is, there is no sin in the unintended oath and no expiation for it. ﴿But He will hold you accountable for what you have bound by oaths﴾: that is, for your binding of the oaths and confirming them by deliberately swearing, that is, when you break them. Or [it means] for breaking what you have bound, and the object is omitted because it is known. It has been read with the lighter form (ʿaqqadtum with a single stress), and it has been read as (ʿaqadtum), which has the same meaning as ʿaqadtum. ﴿Its expiation﴾: that is, the expiation for breaking it, that is, the act that erases its sin: ﴿is feeding ten needy people﴾, meaning poor people in need and those who do not have what suffices them. ﴿From the average of what you feed your families﴾: that is, not from the best of it, let alone what you reserve for yourselves, and not from the worst of what you feed them, let alone what you give to the beggar. ﴿Or clothing them, or freeing a slave﴾: that is, freeing her from bondage. ﴿But whoever cannot find﴾: that is, anything of what has been mentioned. ﴿Then fasting for three days﴾ is his expiation. ﴿That﴾, that is, what has been mentioned, ﴿is the expiation of your oaths﴾: that is, the oaths by which you have presumed against Allah, Exalted is He. ﴿When you have sworn﴾: that is, and broken them. ﴿And guard your oaths﴾: that is, against excessive swearing, or against breaking them, when what you swore to is not good, so that the glorification of Allah's name does not leave your hearts. ﴿Thus﴾: that is, like this complete explanation. ﴿Allah makes clear to you His verses﴾ (p. 2135): that is, the signs of His laws. ﴿That you may be grateful﴾: that is, for His blessing in what He teaches you and eases for you as a way out.

Al-Mahayimi said: That is, you may be grateful for His blessings by directing them to what they were created for. Among them is directing the tongue, which was created for the remembrance of Allah and glorifying Him, toward that. So if the redirecting of some of what one owns to some means that compensates for it fails, so that it may stand in place of gratitude by the tongue, since through it His glorification is completed, then if one does not find [the means], one breaks the desire of the soul for His sake, and this too is glorification of Him. So understand.

There are several discussions concerning this verse:

The first: The meaning of "or" (aw) is choice, and the obligation of one of the three expiations. If one cannot find [the means], one moves on to fasting.

As for feeding, there is no specified quantity in it, neither for one meal nor two, nor for any measure of volume. For this reason there are various reports from the Companions and the Successors concerning it, all of which fall under its general meaning, so whichever one takes is sufficient. Among them is what Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from ʿAli (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "He feeds them at midday and in the evening." It seems that he (may Allah be pleased with him) intended the complete feeding, namely the daily sustenance, which is two meals; otherwise feeding applies to a single meal.

For this reason al-Hasan and Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah said: It suffices that he feed them one meal of bread and meat. Al-Hasan added: If he cannot find it, then bread and clarified butter and milk, and if he cannot find that, then bread and oil and vinegar, until they are satisfied.

It is also reported from ʿUmar, ʿAli, ʿAʾishah, and a group of the Successors: He feeds each one of the ten half a ṣāʿ of wheat or dates or the like.

And from Ibn ʿAbbas: For each needy person, one mudd of wheat, along with its condiment.

(p. 2136) In Fath al-Qadir, from the books of the Hanafis: It is permissible that he feed them at lunch and dinner with bread. However, if it is wheat, condiment is not required, but if it is other than that, then with condiment. It is related from al-Hadi that eating is a condition, because the word "feeding" (al-itʿam) implies this.

Most scholars hold that eating is not a condition, because the word "feeding" applies to transferring ownership.

The second: The general term "needy" (al-masakin) includes the believer, the protected non-Muslim (dhimmi), and the wicked. Some have taken this in its general sense. The school of al-Shafiʿi and the Zaydiyyah hold that the non-Muslim is excluded by analogy with prohibiting the giving of zakat to him. As for the wicked, it is permissible to give to him as long as there is no assistance to him in wrongdoing. Al-Hadi did not permit it. The apparent meaning of the verse requires the number to be ten needy persons. As for the saying of some that the intention is to provide food that suffices ten, and on that basis allowing the feeding of one needy person for ten days, this is a departure from the apparent meaning, which is not established except by a text.

The third: The verse does not specify the limit or description of clothing. Therefore what is obligatory is to interpret it by what the name "clothing" applies to.

Al-Shafiʿi, may Allah have mercy on him, said: If he gives each one of the ten what truly counts as clothing, such as a shirt, trousers, a waist-wrap, a turban, or a face-covering, that suffices him.

Malik and Ahmad ibn Hanbal said: He must give each one of them the clothing with which it is valid for him to pray, whether he is a man or a woman, each according to his situation.

Al-ʿAwfi reported from Ibn ʿAbbas: a cloak for each needy person, or a shamlah (wrap).

Mujahid said: The least is a garment, and the highest is whatever you wish.

From Ibn al-Musayyab: a turban with which he wraps his head, and a cloak with which he covers himself.

From al-Hasan and Ibn Sirin: two garments for each.

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from ʿAʾishah, "from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) regarding His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿or clothing them﴾, he said: a cloak for each needy person." Ibn Kathir said: This is a gharib hadith.

(p. 2137) I say: The caution, and taking the most complete and best option in feeding and clothing, is not hidden.

The fourth: Al-Razi said: What is meant by "a neck" (raqabah) is the whole person. It has been said that the origin of this metaphor is that among the Arabs a captive's hands were tied to his neck with a rope. When he was released, the rope was undone, so the release from the neck was called "unbinding the neck." Then this was applied to manumission. Abu Hanifah took its unrestricted sense and said: A disbelieving female slave is valid, just as a believing female slave is valid. Al-Shafiʿi and others said: She must be a believer. They took the restriction from the expiation for killing, because the obligating cause is unified even though the cause differs. And from the hadith of Muʿawiyah ibn al-Hakam al-Sulami, which is in the Muwatta of Malik, the Musnad of al-Shafiʿi, and Sahih Muslim (p. 2138): "that he mentioned that he owed the freeing of a neck, and he came with a black slave girl. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to her: Where is Allah? She said: In the sky. He said: Who am I? She said: You are the Messenger of Allah. He said: Free her, for she is a believer..." and the hadith in its full length.

Al-Shaʿrani, may his secret be sanctified, said in al-Mizan: The scholars said: The non-consideration of faith in the slave is problematic, because the fruit of manumission is the liberation of a person for the worship of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. If one frees a disbelieving slave, one has only freed her for the worship of Iblis. Also, manumission is an act of nearness (to Allah), and it is not fitting to draw near to Allah through a disbeliever. End of quotation.

The fifth: The scholars differ regarding the limit of hardship that permits moving on to fasting. The apparent meaning of the verse is that one does not possess the means of any of the three expiations: feeding, clothing, or freeing. If one finds the means for one of them, that prevents fasting, unless the surplus is beyond his own food and the food of his dependents on that day.

Ibn Jarir reported from Saʿid ibn Jubayr and al-Hasan that they said: Whoever has three dirhams is obligated to feed; otherwise he fasts.

The sixth: The absolute wording of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿then fasting three days﴾ applies both to consecutive and separate days, as in the making up of Ramadan, because of His saying: ﴿then a number of other days﴾ [al-Baqarah: 185]. Whoever requires consecutiveness relies on the reading of Ubayy ibn Kaʿb and ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud, that they used to recite: "Then fasting three days, consecutively." Their reading does not differ from their narration.

Al-Aʿmash said: The companions of Ibn Masʿud used to recite it that way.

Ibn Kathir said: And this, if it is not established that it is Qur'an by mass transmission, then at least it is an individual report or an exegesis from the Companions, and it has the status of a marfuʿ (attributed to the Prophet) report.

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: "When the verse of expiations was revealed, Hudhayfah said: O Messenger of Allah! Are we free to choose? He said: You are free to choose. If you wish, you free; if you wish, you clothe; and if you wish, you feed. Whoever cannot find [the means], then fasting three consecutive days." Ibn Kathir said: This is a very gharib hadith.

Some of the Zaydiyyah transmitted a report from Ibn Jubayr that he would sometimes pray with the reading of Ibn Masʿud and sometimes with the reading of Zayd.

The seventh: Al-Nasir said in al-Intisaf: In this verse, namely His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿That is the expiation of your oaths when you have sworn﴾, there is a subtle point of derivation regarding the validity of expiation occurring after the oath and before breaking it, which is the well-known position of the school of Malik. The argument from it is that He made what comes after the swearing the time for the occurrence of expiation recognized by the law, since He used "idha" (when) with mere swearing. The verse does not impose expiation, so that one could say: it is agreed that it is only due upon breaking. Therefore it is necessary to interpret it as attached to the swearing. Rather, it only affirms the legality of expiation and its occurrence in a manner of consideration, since His saying "That is the expiation of your oaths" does not give an obligation, but gives validity and consideration. And Allah knows best.

(p. 2140) This is a defense against the prohibition of expiation before breaking absolutely, even if the oath concerns something righteous.

The three positions in the school of Malik are all there, except that the strongest position is the well-known one. End of quotation.

Al-Razi said: Al-Shafiʿi argued from this verse that expiation before breaking is permissible, because it indicates that each of the three is an expiation for the oath when the swearing exists. If he performs it after swearing and before breaking, he has performed the expiation. His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿when you have sworn﴾ contains a subtle point, which is an indication that advancing the expiation before the oath is not permissible. End of quotation.

In the two Sahihs, from the hadith of ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Samurah, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to me: When you swear an oath and you see something else that is better than it, then expiate for your oath and do what is better." In Abu Dawud: "Expiate for your oath, then do what is better."

The eighth: Al-Suyuti said in al-Iklil: In His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿and guard your oaths﴾ there is the recommendation to avoid breaking them unless breaking is good, in accordance with the hadith of Ibn Samurah mentioned above. This is one of two interpretations of the verse. The other is the prohibition of excessive swearing, as previously mentioned. Kuthayyir said:

Few are his oaths; he guards his oath, and even if an oath slips from him, he is pious (his oath is fulfilled).

The ninth: The wisdom in giving precedence to feeding over freeing, even though freeing is more excellent, is from several aspects:

One of them: an alert from the beginning that this expiation is obligatory by choice, not by sequence. Otherwise one would begin with the most severe.

The second: feeding is easier, because it is more widely available, and the purpose of this is to alert that He, Exalted is He, observes leniency and ease in obligations.

The third: feeding is more excellent, because a free poor person may not find food, and there may be no one to give him food, so he falls into harm. As for the slave, it is obligatory upon his master to feed and clothe him. This was reported by al-Razi.

The tenth: The secret of feeding ten: it is like abstaining from food for ten days, the complete number, which breaks the soul that has become bold against Allah, Exalted is He. The secret of clothing is that it compensates for covering the nakedness, the secret of the sin. The secret of manumission is releasing a neck from sin. The secret of fasting three days is that since fasting is by its nature a harm to the self, it suffices with the least plural. This was reported by al-Mahayimi, may his secret be sanctified.

(p-2142) Eleventh: Shams al-Din Ibn al-Qayyim said in Zad al-Ma'ad: The Prophet (ﷺ) would sometimes make an exception (istithna') in his oath, sometimes expiate it (kaffara), and sometimes carry on with it. Istithna' (exception, i.e. saying "in shaa' Allah") prevents the oath from being binding, while expiation (kaffara) releases one from it after it has been taken. For this reason God called it "tahillah" (a release). The Prophet (ﷺ) swore oaths in more than eighty places. God, glorified is He, commanded him to swear in three places. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And they ask you, "Is it true?" Say, "Yes, by my Lord, indeed it is true, and you cannot escape it."﴾ [Yunus: 53] He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And those who disbelieve say, "The Hour will not come to us." Say, "Yes, by my Lord, it will surely come to you."﴾ [Saba': 3] And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Those who disbelieve claim that they will never be resurrected. Say, "Yes, by my Lord, you will surely be resurrected, then you will be informed of what you did, and that is easy for God."﴾ [al-Taghabun: 7]

Isma'il ibn Ishaq al-Qadi used to mention Abu Bakr ibn Dawud al-Zahiri without calling him "al-faqih" (the jurist). One day he and an opponent of his had a dispute brought before him, and the oath was directed at Abu Bakr ibn Dawud. He prepared himself to swear. The judge Isma'il said to him: "You will swear, and someone like you swears, Abu Bakr?" He replied: "What prevents me from swearing, when God, exalted is He, has commanded His Prophet to swear in three places in His Book?" He asked: "Where is that?" So Abu Bakr recited them all, and he (Isma'il) greatly approved of that from him, and from that day he called him "al-faqih." End of quotation.

Commentary on the Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[90] ﴿O you who have believed, indeed, intoxicants, gambling, [sacrificial] stones, and divining arrows are but defilement from the work of Satan, so avoid it that you may be successful.﴾

﴿O you who have believed, indeed, intoxicants﴾ — i.e., the drink that covers the intellect (khamr), meaning it mingles with the intellect and conceals it. ﴿And gambling﴾ — i.e., qimar (games of chance). ﴿And [sacrificial] stones﴾ — i.e., the idols set up for worship. ﴿And divining arrows﴾ — i.e., al-qidah (arrows used for divination). ﴿Are but defilement from the work of Satan﴾ — i.e., an evil product of Satan's adornment, and a filth from which intellects recoil.

Al-Mahayimi said: Because intoxicants destroy the intellect, and what falls short of intoxication calls to that which completes it, so it was placed in the perfect law in its stead. Gambling destroys wealth. The [sacrificial] stones destroy human dignity through a person's humbling himself before what is lower than him. The divining arrows destroy knowledge through ignorance of the price and the thing priced. End of quote.

What he mentioned is only a fragment of their harms.

﴿So avoid it﴾ — i.e., leave it, meaning what has been mentioned. Or [it refers to] the "defilement" (rijs), which applies to all of them. ﴿That you may be successful﴾ — i.e., in hope that you will attain success, thereby being saved from wrath and punishment and being secure in the Hereafter.

Then Almighty God confirmed the prohibition of intoxicants and gambling by explaining their worldly and religious harms. The first is in His words:

[91] ﴿Satan only wants to cause enmity and hatred to arise among you through wine and gambling, and to turn you away from the remembrance of Allah and from the prayer. Will you not then desist?﴾

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

﴿Satan only wants to cause enmity﴾, meaning: mutual abuse, striking, and fighting, ﴿and hatred﴾, which severs the cooperation that a person necessarily needs in his livelihood. ﴿Through wine﴾, meaning: when you become intoxicated. ﴿And gambling﴾, meaning: when your wealth is lost. It has been related that a man might gamble away his family and his children, and when the opponent takes them, enmity arises between the two of them forever. Then He pointed to their religious harms with His words: ﴿and turn you away from the remembrance of Allah﴾, since joy and elation overcome the souls, and immersion in bodily pleasures, so that one is distracted from the remembrance of Allah. As for gambling, if its practitioner is the winner, his soul is delighted, and the love of victory prevents him from the remembrance of Allah. And if he is the loser, because of the constriction and the scheming that arise from his wish to become the winner, (p-2144) the remembrance of Allah does not occur to his mind. ﴿And from the prayer﴾, meaning: and they turn you away from observing its appointed times. His words, exalted is He, ﴿Will you not then desist?﴾ are among the most forceful forms of prohibition, as if it were said: the things in them that divert and hinder you have been recited to you. So will you, with these diversions, desist? Or will you remain as you were, as though you had not been admonished and had not been restrained? This is what al-Zamakhshari conveyed.

Notes (tanbihat):

The first: The discussion of wine and gambling has already occurred in Surat al-Baqarah in His words, ﴿They ask you about wine and gambling﴾ [al-Baqarah: 219]. The meaning of the idols (ansab) and the arrows (azlam) has also already passed at the beginning of this surah at His words, ﴿and what is sacrificed on the stone altars, and that you seek decisions through the arrows﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 3], so recall it.

The second: Wine and gambling were grouped together with the idols and the arrows at first, and then they were mentioned separately at the end, and the explanation of the calamity in them was specifically restricted to them, to draw attention to the fact that the aim is to clarify their condition. The mention of the idols and the arrows is to indicate that they are equal to them in prohibition. It is as if there is no difference between one who worships an idol and associates others with Allah in knowledge of the unseen, and one who drinks wine or gambles.

Al-Harith ibn Abi Usamah narrated in his Musnad, from Ibn 'Amr, traced to the Prophet: "The drinker of wine is like the worshipper of an idol, and the drinker of wine is like the worshipper of al-Lat and al-'Uzza." Its chain is good (hasan).

The singling out of the prayer by mention, although it is included in the remembrance, is for its magnification and to signal that one who diverts from it is like one who diverts from faith, because it is its pillar.

The third: This verse indicates the emphasis on the prohibition of wine and gambling in several respects:

(Among them): The opening of the sentence with (ma), because this word denotes exclusivity (hasr). It is as if He, exalted is He, said: there is no abomination and nothing of the work of Satan except wine and gambling and what is mentioned along with them.

(Among them): He linked them with the worship of idols.

(p-2145) (Among them): He made them an abomination, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿So avoid the abomination of idols﴾ [al-Hajj: 30].

(Among them): He made them from the work of Satan, and nothing comes from Satan except pure evil.

(Among them): He commanded avoiding them, and the apparent meaning of a command is obligation.

(Among them): He made avoiding them part of success. And if avoiding them is success, then committing them is loss and ruin.

(Among them): He mentioned what results from them of calamity, namely the occurrence of mutual hostility and hatred, and what they lead to of turning away from the remembrance of Allah and from observing the times of the prayer.

(Among them): The repetition of the urging to desist in the form of a question, arranged upon what preceded of the kinds of deterrents, by His words, glorified is He, ﴿Will you not then desist?﴾. This indicates that the matter of rebuke and warning, and the exposure of the corruptions and evils in them, has reached its utmost limit, and that excuses have been cut off entirely.

(Among them): His words, exalted is He, after that:

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[92] ﴿And obey Allah, and obey the Messenger, and beware. But if you turn away, then know that the duty of Our Messenger is only clear notification.﴾

﴿And obey Allah and obey the Messenger﴾ means: in all that they have commanded and forbidden. ﴿And beware﴾ means: beware of opposing them in that. Thereby, opposing their command and prohibition regarding wine (khamr) and gambling (maysir) is included, and it is included first and foremost.

Among these is His saying, exalted is He:

﴿But if you turn away, then know that the duty of Our Messenger is only clear notification.﴾ That is: if you turn away from complying with what you have been commanded regarding abstaining from wine and gambling, then the proof (ḥujjah) has been established against you and the excuses have ended. The Messenger has been discharged of the obligation of conveyance (tablīgh), since he has delivered it in a manner beyond which nothing more is required. Nothing remains after that except punishment. In this there is a great threat and a severe warning concerning whoever opposes and turns away from the judgment of Allah and His explanation.

The fourth point: al-Razi said: Know that whoever is fair and abandons obstinacy will know that this verse is a clear text that every intoxicant is prohibited. This is because He, exalted is He, linked the prohibition on drinking wine to its containing those religious and worldly corruptions, and it is known by self-evident reason that those corruptions arise only from its effect in causing intoxication. This establishes with certainty that the cause of His saying, ﴿So will you then desist?﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 91] is that wine has an effect in causing intoxication. When this is established, it is necessary to hold with certainty that every intoxicant is prohibited. He said: Whoever his mind has grasped this argument, yet remains insistent upon his view, there is no remedy for his stubbornness. End of quote.

Then Allah, exalted is He, clarified the lifting of sin from one who died while drinking wine before its prohibition, as we shall detail it, by His saying, glorified is He:

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, may He be exalted:

[93] ﴿There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds for what they have eaten, when they fear Allah and believe and do righteous deeds, then fear Allah and believe, then fear Allah and do good. And Allah loves the good-doers.﴾

﴿There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾ means: no sin, ﴿for what they have eaten﴾ of that which was forbidden after they had consumed it, ﴿when they fear Allah and believe and do righteous deeds, then fear Allah and believe, then fear Allah and do good. And Allah loves the good-doers.﴾

Here are some issues:

The first: Some of the exegetes said: If it is asked, why did He single out the believers for the removal of blame regarding the good things "when they fear Allah," when the disbeliever is the same? Al-Hakim said: Because it is not valid to remove blame from the disbeliever, whereas it is valid to apply it to the believer. And because the disbeliever has closed off for himself the path to knowing what is lawful and unlawful. End of quote.

In al-Inayah: Attaching the removal of blame to these conditions is not meant as a stipulation of them. The absence of blame in consuming what is permitted and not forbidden is not conditional on anything. Rather, it is meant as praise and commendation, indicating that they possess this quality.

Al-Zamakhshari said: An example of this is if someone asks you: "Is there blame upon Zayd for what he did?" and you reply, knowing that it is a permitted matter: "There is no blame upon anyone in what is permitted, if he refrains from the prohibited and is a believer and a good-doer," meaning: Zayd is pious, a believer, and a good-doer, and he is not held accountable for what he did.

Abu al-Su'ud said: Apart from refraining from the forbidden, the other praiseworthy qualities mentioned have no bearing on the removal of blame. They are mentioned within the scope of "when" (idha) as a testimony that those about whom the question was asked possess them, and as praise for them and commendation of their states. This is indicated by the fact that those qualities are made to follow "fearing Allah" each time, to distinguish them from what has a bearing on the ruling. The style of the noble text, by way of expression, although it is to explain the state of those who possess the attributes mentioned concerning what will come later, by virtue of the phrase "idha ma," has nonetheless been expressed as an answer about the state of the past, in order to establish the ruling for them within the general legislation, in a demonstrative manner, through indication of the text, on the basis of their well-known full possession of these qualities. It is as if it were said: There is no blame upon them for what they ate, when they are in obedience to Him, may He be exalted, together with the praiseworthy qualities they have, such that whenever they are commanded to do something, they receive it with compliance. They were consuming wine and gambling in their lives only because they had not yet been prohibited. Had they been prohibited in their era, they would have abstained from them completely.

Al-Tibi said: The meaning is that what is required of the believers is not asceticism from pleasures and the prohibition of good things. Rather, what is required of them is to ascend the stages of piety and faith toward the levels of sincerity and certainty, and the ascents of holiness and perfection. This is by remaining steadfast in refraining from polytheism, in believing in what must be believed, and in righteous deeds, in order to attain complete uprightness, by which one is enabled to ascend to the rank of witnessing and the ascents of (that you worship Allah as if you see Him). This is what is meant by His words, may He be exalted: "and do good," etc. Through it one reaches nearness to Allah and His love. And Allah loves the good-doers.

Al-Khafaji said: This is a response to the question of repetition, and that it is not merely for emphasis, because it would be permissible to join with "then" (thumma), as Ibn Malik explicitly stated in his words: ﴿No! You will come to know﴾ [al-Takathur: 4] ﴿Then, no! You will come to know﴾ [al-Takathur: 4]. Rather, the repetition is in consideration of the difference in what is attached to it each time after another. And Allah knows best.

The second: The "good" mentioned in the verse is either the excellence of action, or excellence toward creation, or the excellence of witnessing previously mentioned. There is no obstacle to understanding it as all of these.

The third: It is narrated concerning the occasion of its revelation from Anas, who said: "I was the cup-bearer of the people in the house of Abu Talha. Then the prohibition of wine was revealed, and the Prophet (ﷺ) commanded a crier, who called out. Abu Talha said: 'Go out and see what this sound is.' He said: So I went out and said: 'This is a crier calling: Verily wine has been prohibited.' He said to me: 'Go and pour it out.' He said: So it flowed through the alleys of Madinah."

He said: Their wine that day was fadikh (a drink made from dates). Some of the people said: "People were killed while it was in their bellies." So Allah revealed: ﴿There is no blame upon those who believe﴾, the verse. Narrated by al-Bukhari in his "Tafsir."

Al-Tirmidhi narrated from al-Bara' ibn Azib, who said: "Some people from the companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) died while drinking wine. When its prohibition was revealed, some people from the companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'What about our companions who died while drinking it?' So it was revealed: ﴿There is no blame upon those who﴾, the verse." He said: Hasan sahih (good and authentic).

And from Ibn Abbas, who said: "They said: 'O Messenger of Allah! What about those who died while drinking wine?' (When the prohibition of wine was revealed), so it was revealed: ﴿There is no blame upon those who﴾, the verse." Al-Tirmidhi narrated it and said: A hadith hasan sahih.

Imam Ahmad narrated from Abu Hurayrah, who said: "Wine was prohibited three times. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to Madinah, they were drinking wine and eating gambling (maysir). They asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about them, so Allah revealed to His Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿They ask you about wine and gambling. Say: In them is great sin and benefit for people, but their sin is greater than their benefit﴾ [al-Baqarah: 219], to the end of the verse. The people said: 'It has not been prohibited for us. He only said: ﴿In them is great sin﴾ [al-Baqarah: 219].' And they continued drinking wine until one day, a man among the Muhajirun led his companions in the Maghrib prayer, and he mixed up his recitation. So Allah revealed a verse more severe than it: ﴿O you who believe! Do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated, until you know what you are saying﴾ [al-Nisa': 43]. So the people would drink until one of them came to prayer while sober. Then a verse even more severe than that was revealed: ﴿O you who believe! Indeed, wine and gambling﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 90], to His words: ﴿So will you not desist?﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 91]. They said: 'We have desisted! Our Lord!' The people said: 'O Messenger of Allah! There are people who were killed in the cause of Allah or died in their beds, who used to drink wine and eat gambling, and Allah has made it an abomination and of Satan's work!' So Allah revealed: ﴿There is no blame upon those who believe...﴾, the verse. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'If it had been prohibited for them, they would have abandoned it, as you abandoned it.'"

Ibn Kathir said: Ahmad alone narrated it.

From Abu Maysarah, who said: When the prohibition of wine was revealed, Umar said: "O Allah! Make clear to us a decisive explanation regarding wine." So the verse in al-Baqarah was revealed: ﴿They ask you about wine and gambling﴾ [al-Baqarah: 219], the verse. Umar was called and it was recited to him. He said: "O Allah! Make clear to us a decisive explanation regarding wine." So the verse in Surah al-Nisa' was revealed: ﴿O you who believe! Do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated﴾ [al-Nisa': 43].
